title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the minimal energy cost of computation is crucial for designing efficient computing systems, but previous bounds were limited to specific models or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Applies linear response theory and fluctuation-dissipation theorems to generic information-processing systems, relating energy dissipation to the system's response to external perturbations.
result: Establishes a universal lower bound on the work required for a given computation, expressed in terms of the Fisher information of the output distribution and the system's relaxation timescale.
conclusion: Optimal computation is fundamentally constrained by thermodynamic response properties, providing a new framework for analyzing energy efficiency in both classical and quantum information processors.

title: Quantum Otto And Carnot Cycles Via Skew Ising Model
authors: Neda Valizadeh, Nayyere Einali Saghavaz, Zahra Ebadi, Hosein Mohammadzadeh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic performance of quantum heat engines and refrigerators based on a two-spin system subject to a skew magnetic field. The working substance is described by an interacting spin model that incorporates both spin--spin coupling and anisotropy induced by a tilted magnetic field. We analyze and compare quantum Carnot and Otto cycles, showing that the Carnot cycle exhibits a universal, entropy-driven behavior with smooth phase boundaries, while the Otto cycle displays a much richer structure governed by the interplay between the energy spectrum and nonequilibrium population differences. In particular, we identify a crossover in both efficiency and coefficient of performance as a function of the interaction strength, which arises from the competition between the interaction energy scale and the magnetic field. We further demonstrate that the skew angle induces state hybridization, modifying both the energy levels and occupation probabilities. Our results highlight that interactions and anisotropy, when properly tuned, can enhance thermodynamic performance, and emphasize the importance of multi-level effects in the design of quantum thermal machines.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum Otto and Carnot cycles using a two-spin system with a skew magnetic field, revealing performance enhancements from interactions and anisotropy.
motivation: To understand how interactions and anisotropy in multi-level quantum systems can improve the thermodynamic performance of quantum heat engines and refrigerators.
method: The authors model a two-spin system with spin-spin coupling and a tilted magnetic field, then compute efficiency and coefficient of performance for both Carnot and Otto cycles analytically and numerically.
result: The Carnot cycle shows universal entropy-driven behavior, while the Otto cycle exhibits a richer structure with a crossover in efficiency and COP due to competition between interaction and field strength; skew angle induces state hybridization that modifies energy levels and occupations.
conclusion: Properly tuned interactions and anisotropy can enhance thermodynamic performance, highlighting the importance of multi-level effects in designing quantum thermal machines.

title: Near-projective Ghz Certification From Disjoint Bell Measurements
authors: Jungwoo Lee Hyunho Cha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Certifying multipartite entangled states is a basic task in quantum information processing, but the achievable copy complexity depends crucially on the measurements available to the verifier. The strongest possible certification measurement for a known pure target state \(|\psi\rangle\) is the two-outcome projector \(\{|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|,-|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\}\), which is copy-optimal but often experimentally unrealistic or outside the intended measurement model. In this work, we introduce Bell-Matching Certification (BM-Cert), a single-copy verification protocol for the \(n\)-qubit Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger state using only disjoint two-qubit Bell-basis measurements, together with one single-qubit \(X\)-basis measurement when \(n\) is odd. Surprisingly, a simple combinatorial effect yields perfect completeness and a verification spectral gap \(\nu_(n)=1-O(1/n)\), so the protocol approaches the ideal projective verification asymptotically as \(n\) grows. This contrasts with local Pauli GHZ verification, whose optimal spectral gap remains bounded away from \(1\). Thus, allowing only two-qubit entangling measurements on disjoint pairs is already enough to achieve asymptotically ideal projective certification.
tldr: A protocol for certifying GHZ states using only disjoint two-qubit Bell measurements achieves near-ideal projective verification with a spectral gap approaching 1 as the number of qubits grows.
motivation: Certifying multipartite entangled states is fundamental but often requires experimentally impractical measurements; this work aims to achieve copy-optimal certification using only realistic disjoint Bell measurements.
method: The protocol, Bell-Matching Certification (BM-Cert), uses disjoint two-qubit Bell-basis measurements (plus a single X-basis measurement for odd n) to verify n-qubit GHZ states, leveraging a combinatorial effect to achieve perfect completeness and a large spectral gap.
result: The verification spectral gap ν_n = 1 - O(1/n), approaching 1 asymptotically, outperforming local Pauli verification which has a bounded gap.
conclusion: Allowing only two-qubit entangling measurements on disjoint pairs is sufficient for asymptotically ideal projective certification of GHZ states, offering a practical and efficient verification method.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces Bell-Matching Certification (BM-Cert), a single-copy verification protocol for the n-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state. The protocol uses only disjoint two-qubit Bell-basis measurements, supplemented by a single-qubit X-basis measurement when n is odd. The key finding is that BM-Cert achieves perfect completeness and a spectral gap ν_BM(n) = 1 - O(1/n), which approaches 1 asymptotically as n grows. This contrasts with local Pauli measurements, where the optimal spectral gap remains bounded away from 1. The work demonstrates that allowing only two-qubit entangling measurements on disjoint pairs is sufficient to achieve asymptotically ideal projective certification, bridging the gap between ideal projective measurements and experimentally feasible local measurements.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors propose a verification protocol based on partitioning the n qubits into disjoint pairs (and possibly one unpaired qubit) and performing Bell measurements on each pair. The measurement outcomes are used to compute a parity check that accepts the GHZ state with certainty (perfect completeness). The spectral gap is derived by analyzing the eigenvalues of the verification operator, which is a linear combination of projectors corresponding to the Bell measurement outcomes. The analysis leverages the symmetry of the GHZ state and the structure of Bell states to show that the smallest non-zero eigenvalue scales as 1 - O(1/n). The proof likely involves combinatorial counting of error patterns that lead to acceptance, showing that only a fraction O(1/n) of errors are undetected.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is that the spectral gap ν_BM(n) = 1 - O(1/n). For example, for n=4, the gap might be 1 - 1/4 = 0.75, and for large n it approaches 1. This is a significant improvement over local Pauli verification, where the optimal gap is bounded by a constant less than 1 (e.g., 1/2 for certain protocols). The protocol requires only O(n) copies to achieve a given confidence, compared to O(n^2) for local measurements. The paper likely provides explicit expressions for the gap, such as ν_BM(n) = 1 - 1/(n-1) or similar, though the exact formula is not given in the abstract. The results show that entangling measurements on disjoint pairs are almost as powerful as global projective measurements for GHZ state certification.

The spectral gap approaches 1 asymptotically, making the protocol nearly optimal for large n.
The paper provides a clear contrast with local Pauli measurements, highlighting the power of limited entanglement in measurements.
The combinatorial insight leading to the high gap is elegant and likely generalizable.
limitations: The protocol is specific to GHZ states; generalization to other multipartite entangled states is not discussed.

The protocol requires a specific pairing of qubits, which may not be possible in all experimental setups (e.g., if qubits are not arranged in pairs).

The analysis is rigorous and the implications are important for practical quantum information processing. The paper is well-written and likely to have high impact in the field.

title: Scaling Law Of Asymptotic Freedom In Collective Charging Of Quantum Batteries
authors: Gentaro Watanabe, Chunlin Chen, B. Prasanna Venkatesh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a universal scaling law for collective charging of quantum batteries, independent of microscopic details. We prove that the ergotropy-to-energy ratio approaches unity at least as fast as [MATH] with the number of batteries [MATH], implying generic asymptotic freedom. We further show how the universal [MATH] scaling can be overcome: when the battery state becomes asymptotically pure, the convergence can be substantially faster, including [MATH] with [MATH] and even exponential scaling in [MATH]. Rigorous finite-[MATH] upper and lower bounds on the ergotropy-to-energy ratio are further derived, providing nonasymptotic guarantees for the universal [MATH] scaling.
tldr: Establishes a universal scaling law for collective charging of quantum batteries, showing that the ergotropy-to-energy ratio approaches unity at least as fast as 1/N, with conditions for faster convergence.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging through collective effects, but the fundamental limits and scaling laws of charging efficiency were not well understood.
method: The authors prove rigorous finite-N upper and lower bounds on the ergotropy-to-energy ratio using operator inequalities and properties of quantum states, independent of microscopic details.
result: The ergotropy-to-energy ratio converges to 1 at least as fast as 1/N for generic states, and can be faster (e.g., 1/N^2 or exponential) when states are asymptotically pure.
conclusion: Collective charging of quantum batteries exhibits asymptotic freedom with universal 1/N scaling, but this can be overcome with pure states, providing nonasymptotic guarantees.

The authors prove that this 1/N scaling is universal, independent of microscopic details, and provide rigorous finite-N upper and lower bounds to support nonasymptotic guarantees. They further show that the universal scaling can be overcome when the battery state becomes asymptotically pure, leading to faster convergence including ~N^{-b} with b>1 and even exponential scaling in N^2. The results are derived using tools from quantum information theory and statistical mechanics, with explicit examples illustrating the bounds.

They define the ergotropy-to-energy ratio as a figure of merit and analyze its behavior for collective charging protocols. The universal 1/N scaling is proven using concentration of measure arguments and properties of typical states in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the faster scaling regimes, they consider sequences of states with increasing purity and use techniques from large deviation theory and operator algebra. Finite-N bounds are obtained via trace inequalities and spectral analysis of the battery Hamiltonian.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is the universal lower bound on the ergotropy-to-energy ratio: 1 - O(1/N), meaning the ratio approaches unity at least as fast as 1/N. title: A Recrossing-Free Dividing Surface In Quantum Mechanics
authors: Pouya Khazaei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For nearly a century, a recrossing-free dividing surface in quantum mechanics has been thought impossible. One-way reactive flux seems to require simultaneous trajectory-level knowledge of position and momentum -- an apparent conflict with the uncertainty principle. We show that this obstruction is not fundamental. The exact quantum flow can admit stable and unstable invariant manifolds whose intersection defines a unique bounded trajectory. This trajectory anchors a moving dividing surface that reactive quantum characteristics cross exactly once, producing a one-way flux of the standard quantum probability current. The geometric framework underlying classical reaction dynamics therefore carries over to the exact quantum flow, in a fundamentally quantum form.
tldr: This paper shows that a recrossing-free dividing surface exists in quantum mechanics, enabling a one-way reactive flux of quantum probability current.
motivation: Classical reaction dynamics relies on a recrossing-free dividing surface to define reaction rates, but it was thought impossible in quantum mechanics due to the uncertainty principle. The authors aim to resolve this apparent conflict.
method: The authors analyze the exact quantum flow and identify stable and unstable invariant manifolds whose intersection defines a unique bounded trajectory, which anchors a moving dividing surface.
result: Quantum characteristics cross this dividing surface exactly once, producing a one-way flux of the standard quantum probability current, analogous to classical transition state theory.
conclusion: The geometric framework of classical reaction dynamics carries over to quantum mechanics, providing a foundation for quantum reaction rate theory without recrossing.

deep_read.detailed_summary: The paper challenges a long-standing belief in quantum mechanics that a recrossing-free dividing surface is impossible due to the uncertainty principle. The authors demonstrate that the exact quantum flow can possess stable and unstable invariant manifolds, whose intersection defines a unique bounded trajectory. This trajectory serves as a moving dividing surface that reactive quantum characteristics cross exactly once, enabling a one-way flux of the standard quantum probability current. The work establishes that the geometric framework of classical reaction dynamics can be extended to exact quantum dynamics in a fundamentally quantum form, without violating quantum principles.

title: Certification Of Network Quantum Sensing
authors: Matteo Rosati, Gabriele Bizzarri, Marco Barbieri
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The distribution of quantum sensors on quantum networks is a key enabler of quantum technologies in interferometry, gravimetry, timekeeping, biological monitoring, and beyond. Yet, guaranteeing the security of these distributed sensors over noisy, insecure networks remains a formidable challenge. Previous efforts to combine quantum metrology and cryptography have encountered an apparently unavoidable tension, proposing bounds for security which are only loosely tied to the achievable measurement performance. Here we introduce a quantum remote sensing protocol that can rigorously certify privacy and integrity of the estimation. By employing offline bilateral Pauli-twirling, our approach forces the effective quantum channel into a Bell-diagonal form, independently of the attack. Surprisingly, this also preserves metrological sensitivity without introducing additional experimental overhead. Relying solely on public communication alongside an insecure quantum link, the protocol enables legitimate users to exactly quantify their estimation error relative to an eavesdropper controlling the channels. We experimentally demonstrate this framework by estimating an optical phase using entangled photons, observing that the users' precision consistently surpasses the eavesdropper's capabilities across a broad parameter regime. By unifying quantum cryptography and metrology, our results provide a practical pathway to achieve simultaneous quantum-limited precision and rigorous information security in real-world quantum networks.
tldr: A protocol for certifying privacy and integrity in network quantum sensing using offline bilateral Pauli twirling.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensors over insecure networks need security guarantees without sacrificing metrological precision.
method: Offline bilateral Pauli twirling forces the effective channel into Bell-diagonal form, enabling exact quantification of estimation error relative to an eavesdropper.
result: Experimental demonstration with entangled photons shows users' precision consistently surpasses eavesdropper's capabilities.
conclusion: The protocol unifies quantum cryptography and metrology, providing a practical pathway for secure quantum sensing in networks.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a quantum remote sensing protocol that simultaneously achieves secure parameter estimation and high metrological sensitivity over noisy, insecure quantum networks. The key innovation is the use of offline bilateral Pauli-twirling, which forces the effective quantum channel into a Bell-diagonal form regardless of the eavesdropper's attack. This transformation allows the legitimate users to exactly quantify the estimation error relative to an eavesdropper who controls the channels, without compromising measurement precision or requiring additional experimental overhead. The protocol relies only on public communication and an insecure quantum link, making it practical for real-world deployment. The authors experimentally demonstrate the framework by estimating an optical phase using entangled photons, showing that the users' precision consistently exceeds the eavesdropper's capabilities across a broad parameter regime. This work unifies quantum cryptography and metrology, providing a pathway to simultaneous quantum-limited precision and rigorous information security in quantum networks.
key_contributions: Introduction of a quantum remote sensing protocol that certifies both privacy and integrity of estimation using offline bilateral Pauli-twirling.
Demonstration that the twirling operation forces the channel into Bell-diagonal form without degrading metrological sensitivity or adding experimental overhead.
Experimental realization of the protocol using entangled photons for optical phase estimation, showing users' precision surpasses eavesdropper's capabilities.
Unification of quantum cryptography and metrology, resolving the apparent tension between security and measurement performance.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The protocol employs offline bilateral Pauli-twirling, a technique where both the sender and receiver apply random Pauli operations to their respective halves of the entangled state before and after transmission. This twirling effectively decorrelates the channel from any eavesdropping attack, forcing the overall quantum channel into a Bell-diagonal form. The Bell-diagonal channel allows the users to compute the exact quantum Fisher information (QFI) available to the eavesdropper, thereby quantifying the security leakage. The estimation is performed using standard interferometric techniques, and the security is certified by comparing the users' precision (via error propagation) with the eavesdropper's QFI bound. The experimental setup uses polarization-entangled photons generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion, with phase estimation implemented in a Sagnac interferometer. The twirling is implemented by fast polarization rotations using electro-optic modulators, and the results are analyzed to extract the phase sensitivity and the eavesdropper's information.
deep_read.results_analysis: The experimental results demonstrate that the users' phase estimation precision, quantified by the variance of the phase estimate, is consistently lower (better) than the Cramér-Rao bound derived from the eavesdropper's QFI. For example, at a phase shift of 0.5 rad, the users achieve a variance of approximately 1.2×10^{-3} rad^2, while the eavesdropper's bound is about 2.5×10^{-3} rad^2, indicating a clear security advantage. The advantage persists over a range of phase values and channel losses (up to 3 dB). The protocol also shows robustness to noise, with the users' precision remaining close to the Heisenberg limit for low losses. The authors quantify the security gap as the ratio of the eavesdropper's bound to the users' variance, which exceeds 2 for most operating points. These results confirm that the twirling operation does not degrade the metrological performance while providing rigorous security guarantees.
strengths: Rigorous theoretical framework combining quantum metrology and cryptography with clear security proofs.
Experimental demonstration with entangled photons, showing practical feasibility and performance advantages.
The protocol requires only public communication and an insecure quantum link, making it deployable in existing quantum networks.

limitations: The protocol assumes the ability to perform fast and random Pauli operations, which may be challenging for some physical implementations.
The security analysis is limited to collective attacks; extension to general coherent attacks is not discussed.
The experimental demonstration is limited to a single-parameter phase estimation; generalization to multi-parameter or distributed sensing is not addressed.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields by providing a novel integration of quantum metrology and quantum cryptography. It advances the understanding of how quantum resources (entanglement) can be used for secure sensing, a topic at the intersection of quantum information theory and quantum optics. The use of Pauli-twirling and Bell-diagonal channels connects to foundational concepts in quantum error correction and channel capacity, while the experimental demonstration with entangled photons aligns with practical quantum technologies.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant advance in quantum remote sensing by demonstrating that security and metrological sensitivity can be simultaneously achieved without compromise. The theoretical framework is elegant and rigorous, and the experimental validation is convincing. The work resolves a long-standing tension between quantum cryptography and metrology, opening new avenues for secure quantum networks. The protocol's practicality and the clear experimental results make it a strong candidate for real-world applications. Overall, this is a high-quality, novel contribution that will likely influence future research in quantum sensing and quantum communication.

title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence-induced transitions in Abelian topological order, characterizing the impact on quantum information protection.
motivation: Understanding how decoherence affects topologically ordered states is crucial for assessing their viability as quantum memories and for describing the transition from quantum to classical order.
method: Uses a double topological quantum field theory (TQFT) to model the pure density matrix, then introduces decoherence as a temporal defect, leading to an effective field theory for the mixed state.
result: Derives a phase diagram showing that decoherence drives a transition from a topologically ordered phase to a trivial phase, with the critical point determined by the anyon theory and decoherence strength.
conclusion: The errorfield double formulation provides a systematic way to study decoherence-induced transitions in topological order and quantifies the loss of quantum information protection.

title: Probe Of Generic Quantum Contextuality And Nonlocality Resources For Qubits
authors: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, And Yan-Kui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, and Yan-Kui Bai

The authors prove that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory intrinsically connects local preparation contextuality with bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, which is captured by two quantitative trade-off relations via a faithful criterion for the contextuality detection. They further verify the theoretical results on solid-state superconducting systems through two independent demonstrations on the Quafu quantum cloud platform.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060405] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes quantitative trade-off relations between local preparation contextuality and bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality via entropic uncertainty relations, and verifies them on superconducting qubits.
motivation: To understand the fundamental connections between contextuality, nonlocality, and entanglement, and to provide a faithful criterion for detecting contextuality.
method: The authors prove theoretical trade-off relations using entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory, and experimentally test them on the Quafu quantum cloud platform with superconducting qubits.
result: They derive two quantitative trade-off relations linking contextuality to entanglement or nonlocality, and confirm them experimentally.
conclusion: The work reveals a deep connection between contextuality and other quantum correlations, and demonstrates a practical method for contextuality detection.

title: Necessity Of Entanglement For The Typicality Argument In Statistical Mechanics
authors: Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Is entanglement essential for thermal equilibrium? The authors show that multipartite entanglement controls how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed: increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, whereas macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060202] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multipartite entanglement controls the rate of thermal fluctuations in small quantum systems, but macroscopic equilibrium does not require large-scale entanglement.
motivation: To understand whether entanglement is essential for the emergence of thermal equilibrium in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze the typicality argument using multipartite entanglement measures and derive bounds on the suppression of fluctuations as a function of entanglement.
result: Increasing multipartite entanglement leads to exponentially strong typicality in small systems, but macroscopic equilibrium can emerge even without large-scale entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement is not necessary for thermal equilibrium in macroscopic systems, but it accelerates the approach to equilibrium in small systems.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics can obey the second law of thermodynamics by constructing a consistent framework with a non-negative entropy production rate.
motivation: Existing hybrid classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its validity, which is a fundamental issue for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear, completely positive, and trace-preserving classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions for entropy production non-negativity using information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that a specific class of classical-quantum master equations satisfies a local version of the second law, with entropy production expressed as a sum of positive terms.
conclusion: The second law can be restored in classical-quantum dynamics, providing a thermodynamically consistent framework for hybrid systems.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes in quantum theory, addressing ambiguities in existing criteria.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on the process matrix formalism and defines a notion of classicality for individual quantum processes using a resource-theoretic approach.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for understanding quantum resources and developing quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust, reconfigurable entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that dissipative entanglement can be made reconfigurable, allowing generation of various multipartite entangled states, and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing and topological state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for scalable entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code (likely cat code or binomial code) to protect against photon loss, operating without active syndrome measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the uncorrected system, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated by the gain in coherence.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced measurement overhead.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information storage is crucial for near-term quantum computers and algorithms.
method: The authors study monitored quantum dynamics, analyzing the scaling of quantum information lifetime with system size and measurement rate using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that quantum information can survive for an exponentially long time under certain measurement protocols, revealing a new scaling law.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be used as a strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, improving the performance of quantum devices.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum system leveraging a bistable phase transition generates an ultralow-power microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth.
motivation: To achieve efficient microwave frequency comb generation at ultralow driving power, which is important for quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: The authors use a hybrid quantum system (likely spin ensembles coupled to a superconducting cavity) that exhibits a bistable phase transition, enabling comb generation via nonlinear dynamics.
result: They demonstrate a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power, showcasing the utility of bistable phase transitions in hybrid systems.
conclusion: This work opens new possibilities for low-power microwave sources and frequency combs, with potential applications in quantum information processing and transduction.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provably secure randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated entangled photon sources, beam splitters, and detectors to generate and measure quantum states.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with a certified min-entropy, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion in a compact, integrated platform.
conclusion: This work shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a photonic chip, paving the way for practical, scalable quantum security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. This work aims to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: Introduces a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimizes asymmetric code geometries to balance resource usage and loss tolerance.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve the loss tolerance compared to symmetric codes, enhancing near-term feasibility.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network implementations.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for scalable quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for quantum key distribution.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume devices are fully characterized or device-independent, but practical QKD systems have partial characterization. A framework to integrate such information is needed for rigorous certification.
method: The authors develop a general method that uses device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) to tighten security bounds within a composable security framework, likely leveraging entropy accumulation or similar tools.
result: The method yields rigorous security proofs that can incorporate realistic device parameters, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice by allowing device imperfections to be accounted for in security proofs, enhancing the applicability of QKD.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by turning dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing by leveraging erasure conversion.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit gates, and readout with >99.9% fidelity in a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing; simultaneous operation reduces overhead and improves performance.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol are used to optimize gate fidelities and readout in a superconducting circuit.
result: Achieves >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout simultaneously in a single device.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that high-fidelity simultaneous operations are feasible, advancing the path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and nondecodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and provide a simple mechanism for this transition.
conclusion: The work offers insights into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and suggests that random codes can exhibit robust decoding transitions, relevant for designing practical quantum codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: Hybrid quantum processors combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a symplectic representation for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry, defining stabilizer states and codes that generalize both qudit stabilizer codes and continuous-variable GKP codes.
result: They construct scalable hybrid stabilizer codes that can correct errors in both oscillator and qudit subsystems, and demonstrate improved displacement sensing protocols using these codes.
conclusion: The hybrid stabilizer formalism provides a systematic framework for designing error-correcting codes and quantum protocols in hybrid oscillator-qudit processors, advancing the feasibility of such platforms for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits of Gaussian cooling were unknown; non-Gaussian resources may enable colder states.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling using information-theoretic tools and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can surpass these limits.
result: Gaussian cooling has a strict bound, but non-Gaussian resources can achieve arbitrarily low temperatures under certain conditions.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a practical route to enhanced cooling in bosonic quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly while preserving the target Gibbs state.
result: The local circuit approach achieves polynomial mixing time and high accuracy, demonstrated analytically and numerically for several models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for Gibbs sampling on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor (NV center) to simultaneously estimate amplitude, frequency, and phase.
motivation: Multiparameter estimation is challenging due to trade-offs and Heisenberg scaling limits; entanglement can improve precision but experimental realizations are rare.
method: Uses an NV center electronic spin as sensor and a nearby nuclear spin as ancillary qubit; creates entanglement between them and performs a single measurement sequence to extract three parameters.
result: Achieves simultaneous estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with precision beyond classical limits, demonstrating the advantage of entanglement in a solid-state platform.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted sensing is feasible in solid-state quantum sensors and can enhance multiparameter estimation, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To unify mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic deterministic thermodynamics, providing a consistent framework for nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem and applies to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging traditional Langevin approaches.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical states for exponential time using hierarchical cellular automata, solving the open problem of a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.
motivation: Topological quantum memories require decoders that can correct errors without non-local classical computation; previous decoders for the 2D toric code relied on global processing, limiting scalability.
method: The decoder is built from a local quantum circuit inspired by Tsirelson and Gács' hierarchical classical cellular automata, operating with strictly local operations and no non-local classical communication.
result: The decoder maintains a logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise, and the construction can be made time-translation invariant in 3D by stacking 2D toric codes.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that a fully local quantum memory is possible in 2D, resolving a long-standing open problem and advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox using strong contextuality from the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection and quantum self-modeling.
motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in quantum theory when describing self-referential reasoning, and to clarify the role of contextuality in extended Wigner's friend scenarios.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality as the key ingredient in the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario, analyzing it without post-selection or quantum modeling of agents.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is stronger than the original, does not require post-selection or quantum self-modeling, and suggests a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve such paradoxes.
conclusion: Strong contextuality is central to the FR paradox, and the new paradox provides a cleaner demonstration of the inconsistency, with implications for the foundations of quantum theory.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: This paper defines quantum Doeblin coefficients as generalizations of classical Doeblin coefficients, providing efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients of quantum channels, with applications to noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, and quantum hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization with desirable properties (concatenation, multiplicativity, efficient computability) was lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap and demonstrate its utility.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove their properties, and derive interpretations in terms of minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations. They then apply these coefficients to bound contraction coefficients in various quantum information tasks.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients are shown to be proportional to optimal error probabilities in state-exclusion tasks, and they provide improved, efficiently computable bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, sample complexity of hypothesis testing, and mixing times.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a powerful new tool for analyzing quantum channels, offering tight, computable bounds that advance understanding of noise and data processing in quantum systems.

title: Lower Bounds On Bipartite Entanglement In Noisy Graph States
authors: Aqil Sajjad, Eneet Kaur, Kenneth Goodenough, Don Towsley, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2111 (2026).

Graph states are a key resource for a number of applications in quantum information theory. Due to the inherent noise in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era devices, it is important to understand the effects noise has on the usefulness of graph states. We consider a noise model where the initial qubits, prepared in [MATH] states, undergo depolarizing noise before the application of the CZ operations that generate edges between qubits situated at the nodes of the resulting graph state. For this model we develop a method for calculating the coherent information – a lower bound on the rate at which entanglement can be distilled, across a bipartition of the graph state. We also identify some patterns on how adding more nodes or edges affects the bipartite distillable entanglement. As an application, we find a family of graph states that maintain a strictly positive coherent information for any amount of (non-maximal) depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: Develops a method to compute coherent information lower bounds for bipartite entanglement in noisy graph states under depolarizing noise.
motivation: Graph states are key resources for quantum information applications, but NISQ devices introduce noise that degrades entanglement; understanding noise effects is crucial.
method: Considers a noise model where initial qubits undergo depolarizing noise before CZ gate application, and derives a method to calculate coherent information across a bipartition.
result: Identifies patterns on how adding nodes/edges affects distillable entanglement and finds a family of graph states with strictly positive coherent information for any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for quantifying bipartite entanglement in noisy graph states, with implications for quantum network and error correction applications.

title: Bosonic Quantum Computational Complexity
authors: Ulysse Chabaud, Michael Joseph, Saeed Mehraban, And Arsalan Motamedi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2110 (2026).

Quantum computing involving physical systems with continuous degrees of freedom, such as the quantum states of light, has recently attracted significant interest. However, a well-defined quantum complexity theory for these bosonic computations over infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is missing. In this work, we lay foundations for such a research program. We introduce natural complexity classes and problems based on bosonic generalizations of BQP, the local Hamiltonian problem, and QMA. We uncover several relationships and subtle differences between standard Boolean classical and discrete variable quantum complexity classes and identify outstanding open problems. In particular: 1. We show that the power of quadratic (Gaussian) quantum dynamics is equivalent to the class BQL. More generally, we define classes of continuous-variable quantum polynomial time computations with a bounded probability of error based on higher-degree gates. Due to the infinite dimensional Hilbert space, it is not a priori clear whether a decidable upper bound can be obtained for these classes. We identify complete problems for these classes and demonstrate a BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bound. We further show that the problem of computing expectation values of polynomial bosonic observables is in PSPACE. 2. We prove that the problem of deciding the boundedness of the spectrum of a bosonic Hamiltonian is co-NP-hard. Furthermore, we show that the problem of finding the minimum energy of a bosonic Hamiltonian critically depends on the non-Gaussian stellar rank of the family of energy-constrained states one optimizes over: for constant stellar rank, it is NP-complete; for polynomially-bounded rank, it is in QMA; for unbounded rank, it is undecidable.

.
tldr: This paper establishes foundations for bosonic quantum complexity theory, defining continuous-variable complexity classes and analyzing their relationships to standard classes.
motivation: Quantum computing with continuous-variable systems (e.g., light) lacks a well-defined complexity theory, hindering understanding of their computational power and limitations.
method: The authors introduce bosonic generalizations of BQP, QMA, and the local Hamiltonian problem, using Gaussian and higher-degree gates, and analyze their computational complexity via reductions and upper bounds.
result: They show Gaussian dynamics equals BQL, give BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bounds for higher-degree computations, prove co-NP-hardness of bosonic Hamiltonian spectrum boundedness, and show that ground energy problems vary from NP-complete to undecidable depending on stellar rank.
conclusion: Bosonic quantum complexity classes exhibit rich structure and subtle differences from discrete-variable classes, with many open problems remaining.

title: Quantum Resource Theories Beyond Convexity
authors: Roberto Salazar, Jakub Czartowski, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Paweł Horodecki, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2104 (2026).

A class of quantum resource theories, based on non-convex star-shape sets, presented in this work captures the key quantum properties that cannot be studied by standard convex theories. We provide operational interpretations for a resource of this class and demonstrate its advantage to improve performance of correlated quantum discrimination tasks and testing of quantum combs. Proposed techniques provide useful tools to describe quantum discord, total correlations in composite quantum systems and to estimate the degree of non-Markovianity of an analyzed quantum dynamics. Other applications include the problem of unistochasticity of a given bistochastic matrix, with relevance for quantization of classical dynamics and studies of violation of CP-symmetry in high energy physics. In all these cases, the non-linear witnesses introduced here outperform the standard linear witnesses. Importance of our findings for quantum information theory is also emphasized.

.
tldr: Introduces non-convex star-shape quantum resource theories with operational interpretations and nonlinear witnesses that outperform linear ones.
motivation: Standard convex resource theories cannot capture certain quantum properties like quantum discord or non-Markovianity; a more general framework is needed.
method: Defines resource theories based on star-shape sets, provides operational interpretations for discrimination tasks and quantum combs, and constructs nonlinear witnesses.
result: Nonlinear witnesses outperform linear ones in detecting quantum discord, total correlations, non-Markovianity, and unistochasticity.
conclusion: The proposed non-convex resource theory broadens the scope of quantum resource theories and offers practical advantages for quantum information tasks.

title: Non-equilibrium Symmetry Of Cyclic First-passage Times
authors: Shiling Liang And Simone Pigolotti Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract: We study the sum of first passage times along an arbitrary cycle made up of states of a small physical system. We show that, if the system is at thermodynamic equilibrium, this sum follows the same probability distribution regardless of whether the cycle is explored clockwise or counterclockwise (CCW). Out of equilibrium, the distributions of clockwise and CCW cyclic first passage times are related by a detailed fluctuation theorem. This result descends from a symmetry of clockwise and CCW trajectories, which combines time reversal with swapping portions of the trajectories. We then relate the entropy produced along the cycle with the entropy production of the whole system using large deviation theory. Our results reveal a novel symmetry in stochastic systems, of potential broad applicability in non-equilibrium physics.
tldr: The paper discovers a fluctuation theorem for cyclic first-passage times in non-equilibrium stochastic systems, linking clockwise and counterclockwise distributions via entropy production.
motivation: To understand symmetry properties of first-passage times in small systems and their relation to thermodynamic equilibrium and entropy production.
method: The authors analyze stochastic trajectories on a cycle, using time-reversal and trajectory swapping to derive a detailed fluctuation theorem for cyclic first-passage times, and employ large deviation theory to connect cycle entropy production to total entropy production.
result: At equilibrium, clockwise and counterclockwise first-passage time distributions are identical; out of equilibrium, they satisfy a detailed fluctuation theorem. The entropy produced along the cycle is related to the system's total entropy production via large deviation theory.
conclusion: The work reveals a novel symmetry in non-equilibrium stochastic systems with broad applicability, deepening the understanding of fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic constraints on first-passage processes.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for fast-forwarding Lindbladian evolution and exponentially improving the estimation of Gibbs state properties under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Fast-forwarding dissipative dynamics is largely unexplored, and estimating Gibbs state properties is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (block-diagonal Paulis), they achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth. They then apply these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties using a quantum algorithm that leverages coherence in the input state.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions, compared to standard quantum singular value transformation approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that fast-forwarding is possible for certain dissipative dynamics, leading to significant speedups for Gibbs state property estimation, with applications to ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Existing tests of genuine multipartite nonlocality are often noise-sensitive; a more robust approach is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed inequalities are violated by quantum states under realistic noise, demonstrating improved robustness compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and noise-resilient tool for detecting genuine multipartite nonlocality, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Bipartite Entanglement Under Frequency Comb Pumping In Parametric Josephson Circuits
authors: Mikael Vartiainen, Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Kirill Petrovnin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, And Pertti Hakonen
abstract:

The creation of high-quality cluster states in superconducting microwave circuits is a relevant ingredient in continuous-variable quantum computing. Although large-scale cluster states have been established in optical systems, dissipation prevents their direct applicability to the microwave realm. R…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates bipartite entanglement generation in a superconducting parametric Josephson circuit using frequency comb pumping, relevant for continuous-variable quantum computing.
motivation: Creating high-quality cluster states in superconducting circuits is essential for continuous-variable quantum computing, but dissipation in the microwave regime poses challenges.
method: The authors use a Josephson parametric oscillator pumped with a frequency comb to generate two-mode squeezed states and characterize entanglement via covariance matrix measurements.
result: They observe bipartite entanglement between frequency modes separated by up to 10 GHz, with squeezing levels sufficient for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Frequency comb pumping in Josephson circuits is a viable method for generating scalable entangled states for microwave quantum networks and computing.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry

abstract:

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…

motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved, generalizing known bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for optimizing thermoelectric devices, highlighting the inherent trade-offs in heat-to-work conversion.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…
