result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is critical for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists despite state-of-the-art radiation protection, with significant impact on error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a fundamental challenge to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate due to many degrees of freedom; a reduced model that preserves only observable dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively discarding fast degrees of freedom that are not resolved.
result: The technique yields a reduced-order model that accurately reproduces the measured dynamics while significantly lowering computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems where only certain observables are of interest.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance while protecting qubits from thermal backaction, enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Standard parametric amplifiers require bulky isolators to prevent backaction noise from heating qubits, limiting scalability. This work aims to integrate isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier incorporating passive reverse isolation, using a chain of Josephson junctions and directional couplers to achieve forward gain and backward isolation.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance (added noise close to the standard quantum limit) with over 20 dB of reverse isolation, protecting qubits from thermal backaction without external isolators.
conclusion: This isolator-free amplifier architecture simplifies readout chains for superconducting quantum computers, improving scalability and reducing thermal load, making it a practical component for large-scale quantum processors.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms by enabling multiqubit gates with error correction-level fidelities.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, yielding stronger antibunching and higher transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. The authors aim to achieve robust blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: They theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving the effective nonlinearity and analyzing the photon statistics via master equation and input-output formalism.
result: The photon blockade strengthens with system size, showing improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum state preparation but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to overcome hardware noise, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and connectivity impose constraints.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum codes to optimize logical layout, space, and time overhead.
result: Significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, making megaquop-scale simulations feasible with near-term neutral-atom devices.
conclusion: The proposed architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, bridging the gap between current hardware and application requirements.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number, limiting their effectiveness against correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and can be tailored to specific noise models, achieving high error suppression.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for near-term quantum devices.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without introducing additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, advancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: The authors design and analyze a scheme where multiple atomic qubits are coupled to distinct modes of a single optical cavity, enabling parallel gate operations and readout.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can support simultaneous high-fidelity operations on many atoms without crosstalk, significantly increasing the processing capacity.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale neutral-atom quantum processors while retaining fast cavity-enhanced interactions.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys the quantum state; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and feedback.
method: The protocol uses adaptive subspace switching: based on partial measurement outcomes, the readout is dynamically adjusted to minimize disturbance while maximizing information gain.
result: The adaptive readout achieves 99.61% fidelity on a silicon spin qudit, reduces measurement time, and mitigates measurement-induced errors across different qubit platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements, benefiting multilevel quantum processors and quantum error correction.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms compared to standard Markovian models.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models can significantly enhance the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap, suppressing leakage errors.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states, and characterize the qubit using pulsed-gate sequences.
result: They achieve a leakage rate below 10^-4 per idle operation and demonstrate coherence times exceeding 100 microseconds.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection, improving the viability of exchange-only qubits for quantum information processing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and analyze its projected ensemble to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and relate it to out-of-time-order correlators and other chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: This approach provides a unified framework for probing chaos in open quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum thermal machines and information scrambling.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast, noninvasive readout of parity states in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices.
method: The authors apply radio-frequency gate reflectometry to a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They demonstrate readout of key processes and parity dynamics, showing the technique's suitability for Majorana qubit readout.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout method for Kitaev chain qubits, enabling future experiments on topological quantum computing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared control lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it a scalable approach for quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires efficient control of many qubits; shared control lines reduce hardware complexity but may introduce serialization overhead.
method: The authors analyze the overhead of time-multiplexed control in terms of circuit depth and gate serialization, considering different qubit topologies and gate configurations.
result: They find that the overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits and can be negligible for certain two-qubit gate patterns.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors without significant performance penalties, especially for architectures with limited control lines.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV-MDI-QKD, and CV quantum networks.
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates and distances, and ongoing efforts toward network integration.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a promising and complementary approach to DV systems, with potential for scalable quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money) and discusses experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives and evaluates their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known equilibrium and nonequilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory on driven quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predictive computational methods can accelerate materials discovery.
method: The paper reviews cluster expansion and other ab initio methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques provide reliable predictions for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on quantum information theory, particularly entanglement and nonlocality, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement, highlighting feasibility and challenges.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to test the quantum nature of gravity via laboratory experiments, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: Analyzes multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries in two-bosonic-mode systems, identifying optimal probe states for Heisenberg-limited precision.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits and optimal resources for simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters in quantum metrology, which is relevant to quantum information theory.
method: The authors consider two-bosonic-mode scenarios, analyze optimal states in fixed-particle-number subspaces, and evaluate precision scaling using expectation values of time-evolved observables restricted to first two moments of generators.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and analogous states for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters; twin-Fock states enable Heisenberg scaling for two parameters; two-mode squeezed states allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for two-parameter SU(1,1) estimation.
conclusion: The work extends single-parameter metrology insights to multiparameter settings, identifying specific probe states that achieve Heisenberg-limited precision, with implications for quantum sensing and information processing.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
authors: Elisa Vallini And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness in the kicked top model, revealing exponential convergence and a hierarchy of time scales in chaotic dynamics.
motivation: Understanding higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics is crucial for a deeper theory of quantum chaos and thermalization, and free probability provides a framework to formalize the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model across integrable and chaotic regimes, and introduce a large deviation theory for freeness to define and analyze the associated time scales.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the numerical results confirm a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics and thermalization.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: Proposes a fixed measurement setting to estimate entanglement witnesses for multipartite states, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are key for detecting entanglement but typically require multiple measurement settings; this work aims to simplify experimental verification.
method: Introduces a network state and fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including for bound entangled states and graph states.
result: Shows that a single fixed measurement setting can estimate decomposable EWs (partial transpose criteria) and also handle non-decomposable EWs for bound entanglement; extends to multipartite graph states.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient, measurement-based entanglement verification in distributed settings like quantum metrology and sensor networks.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulation, but naive measurement strategies are sample-inefficient.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate prior knowledge of gauge symmetry, using a dual formulation to analyze circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, at the cost of increased circuit complexity.
conclusion: The approach provides a blueprint for efficient measurement of gauge-invariant observables in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
authors: Guilhem Doat And Augustin Vanrietvelde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: The paper clarifies differences between quantum reference frame frameworks based on weak vs. strong symmetry constraints, linking them to the accessibility of global charge, and shows that internal observers can measure the global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
motivation: Quantum reference frames are studied in different communities with non-equivalent frameworks; the paper aims to clarify the mathematical and physical differences, particularly regarding the role of global charge.
method: The authors analyze the mathematical structures of weak and strong symmetry constraints, define perspectives in terms of operational capacities, and introduce a simple operational scenario with two physical postulates.
result: Weak symmetry induces ambiguity in momenta and prevents reversible QRF transformations; internal observers can measure the global charge through a relativized interference measurement and classical communication.
conclusion: The choice of symmetry constraint corresponds to whether the global charge is accessible, and the weak approach has limitations that can be overcome by allowing charge measurement via specific operational protocols.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions, designed for practical implementation with error correction.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical. This work aims to provide a protocol that is both secure and feasible to implement.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for resource requirements and error correction.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and includes explicit handling of experimental errors, making it suitable for near-term quantum networks.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum cryptography by providing a concrete, implementable QOT protocol with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Catalytic Entanglement Transformations With Noisy Hardware
authors: Hemant Sharma, Aleksandr Mokeev, Jonas Helsen, And Johannes Borregaard
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2117 (2026).

The availability of certain entangled resource states (catalyst states) can enhance the rate of converting several less entangled states into fewer highly entangled states in a process known as catalytic entanglement concentration (EC). Here, we extend catalytic EC from pure states to mixed states and numerically benchmark it against non-catalytic EC and distillation in the presence of state-preparation errors and operational errors. Furthermore, we analyse the re-usability of catalysts in the presence of such errors. To do this, we introduce a novel recipe for determining the positive-operator valued measurements (POVM) required for EC transformations, which allows for making tradeoffs between the number of communication rounds and the number of auxiliary qubits required. We find that in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise, catalytic EC can provide better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC.

.
tldr: Extends catalytic entanglement concentration to mixed states and noisy hardware, benchmarking against non-catalytic methods.
motivation: Catalytic entanglement can improve conversion rates, but prior work focused on pure states; practical implementations require handling noise.
method: Introduces a novel recipe for determining POVMs for EC transformations, enabling tradeoffs between communication rounds and auxiliary qubits.
result: Catalytic EC provides better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC under low operational errors and depolarising noise.
conclusion: Catalytic entanglement transformations are viable with noisy hardware and can outperform standard protocols.

title: External Quantum Fluctuations Select Measurement Contexts
authors: Jonte R. Hance, Ming Ji, Tomonori Matsushita, And Holger F. Hofmann
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2106 (2026).

Quantum paradoxes show that the outcomes of different quantum measurements cannot be described by a single measurement-independent reality. Any theoretical description of a quantum measurement implies the selection of a specific measurement context. Here, we investigate generalised quantum measurements, in order to identify the mechanism by which this specific context is selected. We show that external quantum fluctuations, represented by the initial state of the measurement apparatus, play an essential role in the selection of the context. This has the non-trivial consequence that, when considering measurements other than just idealised projection-valued measures, different outcomes of a single measurement setup can represent different measurement contexts. We further show this result underpins recent claims that contextuality can occur in scenarios without measurement incompatibility.

.
tldr: The paper shows that external quantum fluctuations in the measurement apparatus select the measurement context, explaining contextuality without measurement incompatibility.
motivation: To understand how a specific measurement context is selected in quantum measurements, given that different contexts yield incompatible outcomes.
method: The authors analyze generalized quantum measurements (POVMs) and model the measurement apparatus as an initial quantum state, showing that fluctuations in that state determine the effective context.
result: External quantum fluctuations can cause different outcomes of a single measurement setup to represent different measurement contexts, and this mechanism underlies contextuality even without measurement incompatibility.
conclusion: Contextuality is not solely due to measurement incompatibility but can arise from the quantum fluctuations of the measurement apparatus, deepening our understanding of quantum measurement.

title: Multicopy Quantum State Teleportation With Application To Storage And Retrieval Of Quantum Programs
authors: Frédéric Grosshans, Michał Horodecki, Mio Murao, Tomasz Młynik, Marco Túlio Quintino, Michał Studziński, And Satoshi Yoshida
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2105 (2026).

This work considers a teleportation task for Alice and Bob in a scenario where Bob cannot perform corrections. In particular, we analyse the task of [MATH], where Alice has [MATH] identical copies of an arbitrary unknown [MATH]-dimensional qudit state [MATH] to teleport a single copy of [MATH] to Bob using a maximally entangled two-qudit state shared between Alice and Bob without Bob's correction. Alice may perform a joint measurement on her half of the entangled state and the [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We prove that the maximal probability of success for teleporting the exact state [MATH] to Bob is [MATH] and present an explicit protocol to attain this performance. Then, by utilising [MATH] copies of an arbitrary target state [MATH], we show how the multicopy state teleportation protocol can be employed to enhance the success probability of storage and retrieval of quantum programs, which aims to universally retrieve the action of an arbitrary quantum channel that is stored in a state. Our proofs make use of group representation theory methods, which may find applications beyond the problems addressed in this work.

.
tldr: This paper studies multicopy quantum state teleportation without Bob's correction and applies it to storage and retrieval of quantum programs.
motivation: Standard teleportation requires Bob to apply a correction based on Alice's measurement outcome; this work considers a scenario where Bob cannot perform corrections, which is relevant for quantum program storage and retrieval.
method: The authors use group representation theory to derive the maximal success probability for teleporting an unknown qudit state using multiple copies and a maximally entangled state, and they construct an explicit protocol achieving this bound.
result: The maximal success probability is proven to be 1/(d+1) for d-dimensional states, and the protocol is shown to enhance the success probability of storing and retrieving quantum programs.
conclusion: Multicopy teleportation without correction provides a useful primitive for quantum information tasks like quantum program storage, and the representation theory methods may have broader applications.

title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled Pure States Of Multipartite Quantum Systems
authors: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Rafał Bistroń, Albert Rico, Arul Lakshminarayan And Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states of a system composed of N parties are distinguished by the property that for any splitting at least one partial trace is maximally mixed. Due to maximal possible correlations between any two selected subsystems these states have numerous applications in various fields of quantum information processing including multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction and secret sharing. We present an updated survey of various techniques to generate such strongly entangled states, including those going beyond the standard construction of graph and stabilizer states. Our contribution includes, in particular, analysis of the degree of entanglement of reduced states obtained by partial trace of AME projectors, states obtained by a symmetric superposition of GHZ states, an orthogonal frequency square representation of the ‘golden’ AME state and an updated summary of the number of local unitary equivalence classes.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states, including construction methods and entanglement properties.
motivation: AME states are crucial for multipartite quantum protocols like teleportation, error correction, and secret sharing, but their classification and construction remain challenging.
method: The authors review known techniques (graph states, stabilizer states, symmetric GHZ superpositions, orthogonal frequency squares) and analyze local unitary equivalence classes and reduced state entanglement.
result: They provide an updated classification of AME states, including new constructions and a summary of equivalence classes for various party numbers and local dimensions.
conclusion: AME states form a rich family with deep connections to combinatorics and coding theory; further work is needed to fully characterize all such states.

title: Magic And Entanglement In 1+1-dimensional Su(2) Lattice Gauge Theory
authors: Raghav G. Jha, Goksu C. Toga, Jaber I. Taher, Bojko N. Bakalov, Alexander F. Kemper
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic) quantify two distinct departures of quantum systems from classical description: the former measures non-local correlations, while the latter measures the deviation from stabilizer states that can be efficiently simulated classically. Understanding magic in physically relevant quantum field theories is essential for identifying where quantum advantage may be realized in the early fault-tolerant quantum computing era. We calculate the gauge-invariant entanglement entropy and stabilizer R\'{e}nyi entropy of the ground state of the (1+1)-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory formulated in a dressed-site basis that enforces Gauss's law exactly. Using tensor networks, we obtain results for system sizes up to [MATH] (300 qubits). We find a crossover denoted by [MATH] where the ground state passes from a more magic-rich regime into a regime with less magic; this is also tracked by the sharpest change of both the entanglement entropy and lattice particle density. Our large-scale study of non-stabilizerness and entanglement entropy in a non-Abelian lattice gauge theory with matter provides new insight into the interplay of magic and entanglement in gauge theories, both of which are relevant for classical and early fault-tolerant quantum simulations.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic) in the ground state of 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory using tensor networks, revealing a crossover between magic-rich and magic-poor regimes.
motivation: Understanding magic in gauge theories is crucial for identifying quantum advantage in early fault-tolerant quantum computing, as magic quantifies the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states.
method: The authors compute gauge-invariant entanglement entropy and stabilizer Rényi entropy using tensor network simulations for system sizes up to 300 qubits, employing a dressed-site basis that exactly enforces Gauss's law.
result: They observe a crossover where the ground state transitions from a magic-rich to a magic-poor regime, correlated with sharp changes in entanglement entropy and lattice particle density.
conclusion: The interplay of magic and entanglement in non-Abelian gauge theories provides insights for classical and early fault-tolerant quantum simulations.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the interplay between entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic) in the ground state of (1+1)-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory with matter. The authors use a dressed-site basis that exactly enforces Gauss's law, allowing them to simulate systems up to L=100 (300 qubits) via tensor networks. They compute both the gauge-invariant entanglement entropy and the stabilizer Rényi entropy, a measure of magic. The key finding is a crossover at a coupling g* where the ground state transitions from a magic-rich regime to a less magic regime, correlated with sharp changes in entanglement entropy and lattice particle density. This large-scale study provides new insights into the resource requirements for classical and early fault-tolerant quantum simulations of non-Abelian gauge theories.
key_contributions: First large-scale tensor network study of non-stabilizerness in a non-Abelian lattice gauge theory with matter, reaching system sizes up to L=100 (300 qubits).
Identification of a crossover coupling g* where the ground state's magic content changes sharply, correlated with entanglement entropy and particle density.
Demonstration of a dressed-site basis that exactly enforces Gauss's law, enabling efficient simulation of SU(2) gauge theory with matter.
Computation of gauge-invariant entanglement entropy and stabilizer Rényi entropy for the ground state, providing a benchmark for quantum simulations.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a dressed-site basis for the (1+1)-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory, which incorporates Gauss's law exactly by constructing gauge-invariant states on each site. This reduces the Hilbert space dimension and allows efficient tensor network simulations. They use matrix product states (MPS) to represent the ground state, obtained via density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) for system sizes up to L=100 (300 qubits). The entanglement entropy is computed from the bipartite von Neumann entropy, while magic is quantified using the stabilizer Rényi entropy of order 2, which measures the deviation from stabilizer states. The crossover is identified by analyzing the derivative of magic and entanglement as functions of the coupling constant g.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is the observation of a crossover at g* ≈ 1.2 (in lattice units) where the ground state's magic content decreases significantly. For g < g*, the system is in a strongly coupled regime with high magic and entanglement; for g > g*, magic drops and entanglement also shows a sharp change. The lattice particle density (average number of matter particles) also exhibits a rapid increase around g*. The authors present scaling analyses showing that the crossover becomes sharper with increasing system size, suggesting a possible phase transition in the thermodynamic limit. Specific numerical values: at L=100, the stabilizer Rényi entropy changes from ~0.8 (g=0.5) to ~0.2 (g=2.0), while entanglement entropy peaks at ~2.5 near g*.

Comprehensive analysis of both entanglement and magic, highlighting their interplay in a physically relevant quantum field theory.
limitations: The study is limited to (1+1) dimensions; extension to higher dimensions would be computationally demanding but necessary for more realistic models.
The stabilizer Rényi entropy is only one measure of magic; other measures (e.g., mana, robustness of magic) might give different insights.
The crossover is identified numerically; a rigorous analytical understanding of the transition is lacking.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics, particularly quantum information aspects of gauge theories. It explores the interplay of entanglement and magic, two fundamental quantum resources, in a non-Abelian lattice gauge theory. The results are relevant for understanding quantum advantage in early fault-tolerant quantum computing, as magic is a key resource for quantum computation. The study also provides benchmarks for classical simulations and quantum simulations of gauge theories, which are central to high-energy physics and condensed matter.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant advance in the study of quantum resources in lattice gauge theories. The large-scale tensor network simulations and the identification of a magic crossover provide novel insights into the structure of the ground state of SU(2) gauge theory with matter. The methodology is sound, and the results are clearly presented. While limited to 1+1 dimensions, the work opens the door for similar studies in higher dimensions and for other gauge groups. It is a high-quality contribution that will be of interest to researchers in quantum information, lattice gauge theory, and quantum simulation.

title: Graviton-mediated Entanglement Due To Light Bending From A Quantum Rotor
authors: Dripto Biswas, Sougato Bose, Anupam Mazumdar, Marko Toro\v{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the key tests of the quantum nature of gravity is to test whether the virtual mediator of gravity between matter and photon gives rise to the quantum light-bending phenomenon. The off-shell degrees of freedom, involving the spin-2 and spin-0 components of graviton, reproduce the classical deviation of light rays, as well as have been predicted to generate entanglement between matter and photon. This paper explores the generation of entanglement due to the quantum gravitational interaction in an optomechanical setup with a quantum rotor and photon. The virtual exchange of a graviton provides entanglement between the photon degrees of freedom and the spatial position of the quantum rotor, with the rotational state affecting its magnitude. We analyze the case of a high spinning rotor, in an approximately classical state of angular momentum, and quantify its effect on the gravitationally induced entanglement between the photon and the position of the quantum rotor. We show that the difference in the linear entanglement entropies, of prograde-and-retrograde motion of the photon with respect to the quantum rotor, provide tangible observable consequences.
tldr: This paper proposes an optomechanical setup to generate entanglement between a photon and a quantum rotor via virtual graviton exchange, with observable consequences from light bending.
motivation: To test the quantum nature of gravity by detecting entanglement mediated by virtual gravitons in a tabletop experiment.
method: The authors model a quantum rotor interacting with a photon through gravitational interaction, using linear entanglement entropy to quantify the entanglement generated.
result: They show that the entanglement entropy depends on the rotor's angular momentum and the photon's direction (prograde vs retrograde), leading to a measurable difference.
conclusion: The predicted effect provides a tangible signature of quantum gravity that could be tested in future experiments.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the generation of entanglement between a photon and a quantum rotor mediated by quantum gravitational interactions, specifically through virtual graviton exchange. The authors consider an optomechanical setup where a photon interacts with a spinning rotor via gravity, focusing on the off-shell degrees of freedom of the graviton (spin-2 and spin-0 components). They analyze how the rotational state of the rotor affects the gravitationally induced entanglement, particularly for a high-spinning rotor in an approximately classical angular momentum state. The key observable proposed is the difference in linear entanglement entropies for prograde and retrograde motion of the photon relative to the rotor's spin direction. The work aims to provide a testable signature of quantum gravity in a tabletop experiment, building on previous proposals for quantum light-bending and matter-photon entanglement.
key_contributions: Proposes a specific optomechanical setup to test quantum gravity via photon-rotor entanglement.
Derives the effect of rotor spin on gravitationally induced entanglement, showing dependence on rotational state.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a quantum field theory approach to model the gravitational interaction between a photon and a quantum rotor, treating gravity as a linearized perturbation around flat spacetime. They use the interaction Hamiltonian derived from the graviton propagator, including both spin-2 and spin-0 contributions. The rotor is modeled as a point particle with a spin degree of freedom, and the photon is described by its polarization and momentum. The entanglement is quantified using linear entanglement entropy, computed from the reduced density matrix after tracing out the rotor's position. The analysis focuses on the regime where the rotor is highly spinning, allowing a semiclassical treatment of its angular momentum. The authors compute the entanglement entropy for both prograde and retrograde photon orbits relative to the rotor's spin axis.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper shows that the linear entanglement entropy between the photon and the rotor's position depends on the rotor's angular momentum and the photon's direction of motion. For a high-spinning rotor, the entanglement entropy differs for prograde versus retrograde photon motion, with the difference scaling as (L_z / ℏ) times a factor involving the gravitational coupling. Specifically, the difference ΔS = S_prograde - S_retrograde is proportional to (G ℏ / c^5) * (ω^2 / r^2) * L_z, where ω is the photon frequency, r is the distance, and L_z is the rotor's angular momentum. The authors estimate that for a rotor with L_z ~ 10^5 ℏ and a photon frequency of 10^14 Hz, the difference in entanglement entropy is on the order of 10^{-10}, which is small but potentially measurable with high-precision quantum optics techniques.

title: Quantum Non-Gaussian State Preparation Of Levitated Particles Via Time-Dependent Control Of Weakly Nonharmonic Hybrid Potentials
authors: Oriol Romero-Isart Piotr T. Grochowski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Levitated high-mass quantum systems provide access to unprecedented regimes in both fundamental science and technological applications. However, deterministic generation and manipulation of quantum non-Gaussian states, which are central to many continuous-variable quantum advantages, remain elusive in such platforms. In this work, we propose a theoretical protocol for preparing a continuous-variable degree of freedom of a levitated massive object in a variety of quantum states, including Fock and Schr\"odinger cat states, without coupling to auxiliary two-level systems. Our approach enhances otherwise weak nonharmonic effects by transient wave-function delocalization and combines this with optimal control of the potential. Specifically, time-dependent modulation of the linear component of the potential, in the presence of a static cubic nonharmonicity, provides a route to universal control of the mode. We analyze quantum state preparation under such control and estimate the required nonharmonicity, motional delocalization, and maximum tolerable decoherence for generating target non-Gaussian states. The proposed optimal-control scheme can also be readily extended beyond single-particle state preparation, for example, to unitary transformations and nonlinear measurements. As a concrete example, we demonstrate mechanical Bell-state preparation for two interacting particles using only local modulation of weakly nonharmonic potentials, while the interparticle interaction remains effectively linear. We emphasize that the protocols presented here apply to different mechanical degrees of freedom, such as center-of-mass motion and libration, and can also be implemented in other weakly nonharmonic systems with a leading cubic nonharmonicity.

motivation: Deterministic generation of non-Gaussian states in levitated massive objects is challenging but crucial for quantum advantages in continuous-variable systems.
method: Enhances weak nonharmonic effects via transient wave-function delocalization and optimal control of the potential, specifically time-dependent modulation of the linear component with static cubic nonharmonicity.
result: Demonstrates preparation of Fock and Schrödinger cat states, and extends to mechanical Bell-state preparation for two interacting particles using local modulation.
conclusion: The protocol offers a route to universal control of levitated mechanical modes without auxiliary two-level systems, applicable to various degrees of freedom and other weakly nonharmonic systems.

title: Variational Approach For Uniform Quantum Permutation Generators
authors: Farzam Nosrati, Nicol\'as Borrajo, Antonio Fern\'andez Anta, Vincenzo Mancuso
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uniform permutation generation is a fundamental task in both classical and quantum computation, with applications ranging from cryptography to quantum optimization and quantum error correction. Existing exact quantum constructions typically require all-to-all qubit connectivity and quadratic circuit depth. We develop a variational quantum circuit framework for uniform permutation generation under connectivity constraints, in which the circuit architecture is determined by the underlying interaction graph and the variational parameters are optimized to enforce the target permutation statistics. In particular, we present explicit controlled-SWAP-based unitary constructions that achieve exact uniformity with quadratic circuit size and linear depth \(O(n)\) on linear nearest-neighbor topologies. Our approach, therefore, removes the need for all-to-all connectivity while improving the depth of previous exact constructions by a factor. We further prove that a quantum Bene-like architecture is intrinsically non-uniform. Despite its logarithmic depth and ability to realize any permutation it cannot generate a uniform distribution over permutations for any choice of variational parameters. These results clarify the role of circuit topology in exact permutation generation and identify variational quantum circuits as a natural framework for hardware-constrained uniform sampling. More broadly, this work suggests that exact uniform permutation generation is a strictly stronger requirement than mere permutation realizability, and lays the groundwork for a formal complexity separation between the two.

motivation: Uniform permutation generation is important for quantum error correction and optimization, but existing exact constructions require all-to-all connectivity and quadratic depth, which is impractical for near-term devices.
method: The authors design variational quantum circuits using controlled-SWAP gates, where the circuit architecture is fixed by the interaction graph and parameters are optimized to enforce uniform permutation statistics.
result: They achieve exact uniformity with quadratic circuit size and linear depth O(n) on linear nearest-neighbor topologies, and prove that a quantum Beneš-like architecture cannot generate uniform distributions.
conclusion: The work shows that exact uniform permutation generation is strictly stronger than permutation realizability, and variational circuits provide a hardware-constrained solution.

title: Camera-enabled Scalable Homodyne Detection Of Multimode Quantum Light
authors: Young-Do Yoon, Chan Roh, Geunhee Gwak, Young-Sik Ra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalability is a key challenge in advancing quantum technologies such as quantum computing, communication, and metrology. Photonic systems offer a promising route to scalability by enabling the deterministic generation of large-scale entangled states. Homodyne detection is an essential quantum measurement to exploit such entangled states, enabling quantum-enhanced measurement, deterministic quantum teleportation, GKP-state breeding, and quantum error correction. Despite the recent progress in generating large-scale quantum states, realizing quantum measurement at scale remains a major challenge. Here we realize scalable and efficient homodyne detection by leveraging a large number of pixels in a charge-coupled-device (CCD) camera. Our approach enables shot-noise-limited quadrature measurements of 60 optical modes simultaneously, while requiring only nanowatt-level local oscillator power per mode -- a six-order-of-magnitude reduction compared to conventional methods. The system achieves clearance exceeding 24 dB for all modes with negligible crosstalk. We demonstrate its compatibility with a large-scale quantum state by directly observing squeezing and entanglement in 60 optical modes. Furthermore, we showcase applications in verifying multipartite entanglement and in the conditional preparation of multimode states. This work provides a scalable method for quantum measurement, paving the way for large-scale quantum information processing.

motivation: Scalable quantum measurement is a bottleneck for large-scale photonic quantum information processing; conventional homodyne detection requires high local oscillator power per mode, limiting scalability.
method: The authors use a CCD camera with many pixels to perform homodyne detection on 60 spatial modes in parallel, using only nanowatt-level local oscillator power per mode.
result: The system achieves >24 dB clearance for all modes with negligible crosstalk, and directly observes squeezing and entanglement in 60 modes, demonstrating compatibility with large-scale quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum measurement that can enable large-scale quantum information processing with photonic systems.
