title: Ultra-high Q-factor Superconducting Tantalum Resonators On 300 Mm Si Wafers
authors: R. Acharya, D. Perez Lozano, Ts. Ivanov, S. Massar, C. Vrancken, Y. Canvel, Y. Li, A. M. Vadiraj, J. van Damme, S. Aghaeimeibodi, A. Khalajhedayati, M. Mongillo, O. Painter, D. Wan, A. Poto\v{c}nik, K. de Greve
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting resonators are central to superconducting quantum information technologies and essential for bosonic qubit architectures, where long-lived storage modes enable hardware-efficient error correction. Achieving ultra-high quality factors in scalable planar circuits is challenging because multiple dissipation channels contribute to the total loss. Here we report planar [MATH]-Ta resonators fabricated on 300 mm ultra-high-resistivity ([MATH] k[MATH] cm) intrinsic silicon using industrial processes, achieving median internal Q factors exceeding 40 million and maxima above 60 million. Energy-participation-ratio analysis identifies a dominant participation-controlled interface loss mechanism and places conservative upper bounds on substrate-associated dissipation. For the best-performing substrate, the inferred substrate loss tangent is below [MATH], establishing industrial MCZ silicon among the lowest-loss substrate platforms reported for superconducting resonators. At the same time, the exceptionally low losses show no clear correlation with commonly cited silicon substrate metrics such as room-temperature resistivity or impurity concentrations. More broadly, these studies establish industrial 300 mm processing, careful interface engineering, and 300 mm MCZ silicon substrates as a promising platform for resonator-heavy superconducting quantum architectures with ultra-high quality factors.
tldr: Demonstrates ultra-high Q-factor superconducting tantalum resonators on 300 mm silicon wafers using industrial processes, with median internal Q exceeding 40 million.
motivation: Achieving ultra-high quality factors in scalable planar superconducting resonators is crucial for bosonic qubit architectures and hardware-efficient error correction, but multiple dissipation channels limit performance.
method: Fabricated planar tantalum resonators on 300 mm ultra-high-resistivity intrinsic silicon using industrial CMOS-compatible processes, and performed energy-participation-ratio analysis to identify loss mechanisms.
result: Median internal Q factors >40 million (max >60 million), with interface loss as dominant mechanism; substrate loss tangent below 10^-6 for best substrates.
conclusion: Industrial 300 mm processing with careful interface engineering and MCZ silicon provides a promising platform for ultra-high-Q superconducting resonators for quantum computing.

title: Equation Asymmetry: An Algebraic Framework For Unifying Secrecy And Covertness In Information-Theoretic Security
authors: Zhang Kuang Wang Hao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the algebraic structure underlying a broad class of information-theoretic security problems. We define the equation asymmetry degree (EAD) as [MATH], where [MATH] is the signal embedding dimension and [MATH] is the effective rank of the adversary's observation matrix. This single parameter is shown to simultaneously govern both secrecy (measured by equivocation [MATH]) and covertness (measured by detection error probability [MATH]). On finite fields [MATH], we establish the equivocation lower bound [MATH] with exact probabilistic conditions (Theorem~1), the secrecy capacity [MATH] with complete achievability and converse proofs (Theorem~2), and a strong converse (Theorem~8). In the continuous Gaussian regime, we derive a differential-entropy equivocation bound (Lemma~1), the high-SNR secrecy capacity asymptotics (Lemma~2), and a 2-Wasserstein distance covertness condition [MATH] (Theorem~5'). The EAD-SDoF equivalence [MATH] is established (Theorem~7). Both [MATH] and [MATH] are shown to be monotone functions of [MATH] (Theorem~6), with a Pearson correlation of [MATH] in continuous-domain experiments. Seven existing security schemes -- matrix embedding, MIMO wiretap, secure network coding, FRFT multi-angle transmission, traffic steganography, group-key secure summation, and MDS secure summation -- are unified under the common form [MATH]. Post-quantum security follows from the information-theoretic hardness of underdetermined linear systems (Theorem~9). All numerical experiments are reproducible with open-source code.
tldr: Introduces equation asymmetry degree (EAD) as a unifying algebraic framework for information-theoretic secrecy and covertness.
motivation: To unify diverse security schemes (e.g., wiretap, steganography, secure network coding) under a common algebraic structure and derive fundamental limits.
method: Defines EAD based on signal embedding dimension and adversary's observation rank; proves equivocation bounds, secrecy capacities, and covertness conditions for finite fields and Gaussian channels.
result: Establishes that both secrecy (equivocation) and covertness (detection error) are monotone functions of EAD, with high correlation in experiments; unifies seven existing schemes.
conclusion: EAD provides a single parameter governing both secrecy and covertness, offering a unified perspective and potential for post-quantum security via underdetermined linear systems.

The paper provides rigorous results for both finite fields and continuous Gaussian channels. On finite fields, it establishes exact equivocation bounds, secrecy capacity C_s = (n - r_E) log q with achievability and converse, and a strong converse. In the Gaussian regime, it derives differential-entropy bounds, high-SNR secrecy capacity asymptotics, and a 2-Wasserstein distance covertness condition. The EAD is shown to be equivalent to the secrecy degrees of freedom (SDoF) via d_s = n·Φ, and both secrecy and covertness metrics are monotone functions of Φ with a Pearson correlation of 0.997 in experiments. The framework unifies seven existing security schemes under the common form C_s = (n - r) log q, and post-quantum security is argued via the hardness of underdetermined linear systems.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
authors: Jing Qiu

tldr: An integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with ITU channel grid for quantum networking.
motivation: To enable scalable wavelength-division multiplexing in quantum networks, a high-quality multi-wavelength photon source aligned with standard telecommunication channels is needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate an integrated photonic chip that generates multiple quantum-correlated photon pairs at ITU grid wavelengths using nonlinear optics.
result: The source achieves high brightness, low noise, and compatibility with ITU channel grid, demonstrating multi-wavelength quantum light generation on a single chip.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable light source for future quantum networks, facilitating multiplexed quantum communication.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
authors: Gaurav Saxena
Thi Ha Kyaw
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant runtime error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is less sensitive to noise.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require significant overhead. The authors aim to reduce runtime while maintaining effectiveness.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a carefully chosen subspace, using a combination of circuit recompilation and post-selection to suppress errors without full error correction.
result: Demonstrates that the restricted evolution approach can achieve error mitigation with constant runtime overhead, independent of circuit depth, and shows improved fidelity on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The technique offers a practical, low-overhead error mitigation strategy suitable for near-term quantum processors, though it may not be universally applicable to all circuits.

tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with spin resolution.
motivation: To achieve programmable assembly of fermionic atoms in optical tweezers for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers and spin-resolved imaging with large differential magnetic moments to prepare arbitrary two-component product states.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for 6×6 arrays.
conclusion: This platform enables high-fidelity fermionic quantum simulation and computation with neutral atoms.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, leading to rapid thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how disorder can protect against heating in driven quantum systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases, but the robustness of this protection under realistic multi-frequency driving is unknown.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain driven by two incommensurate frequencies using numerical simulations and analytical arguments, analyzing heating rates and prethermal lifetimes.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced prethermal plateau, causing the system to heat rapidly even when each frequency alone would be suppressed by disorder.
conclusion: Disorder-suppressed heating is fragile to multi-frequency driving, which has implications for Floquet engineering in quantum simulators and quantum computing platforms.

method: The authors theoretically analyze a dimer of qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements, using stochastic master equations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that strong measurements induce a quantum Zeno effect that confines the dynamics to a subspace, and that correlations between measurements can lead to novel dark states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into measurement-induced phenomena and their potential for controlling quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

result: The proposed gate achieves operation times significantly shorter than the tunneling time while maintaining high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to faster two-qubit gates in neutral atom platforms, enhancing their viability for quantum information processing.

method: A four-level atom strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide enables resonant four-wave mixing, converting an incoming photon into a Stokes and anti-Stokes pair.
result: The scheme achieves generation rates, state purities, and cross-correlations that match or exceed current techniques.
conclusion: Chiral waveguide QED provides a promising platform for deterministic photon-pair generation with high performance.

motivation: Exact master equations for multistate/multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Employs an equation-of-motion approach to derive exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double excitations.
result: Obtains exact master equations that capture double-excitation dynamics, enabling accurate description of dissipative processes in the model.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex quantum dissipative dynamics in multistate systems, relevant for circuit QED and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays

motivation: The MIS problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require large atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to embed arbitrary graphs, leveraging the van der Waals interaction to encode the MIS constraint with fewer atoms.
result: The 3D embedding reduces the atom overhead compared to 2D schemes, enabling the encoding of larger graphs with the same number of atoms.
conclusion: This work provides a more efficient mapping for quantum optimization on Rydberg platforms, advancing the practical implementation of quantum algorithms for NP-hard problems.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen

The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…

method: The authors analyze the effect of detection inefficiency on the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria, deriving conditions for successful detection and comparing their tolerance to the loophole.
result: The PPT criterion can detect a larger volume of entangled states than moment-based criteria in ideal setups, and this advantage persists under the detection loophole, though both are affected.
conclusion: The PPT criterion is more robust to detection inefficiencies, making it preferable for practical entanglement detection.

result: They demonstrate that measurement records can encode signatures of emergent phenomena, such as phase transitions or dynamical phases.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for revealing emergent many-body physics, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

method: The authors derive explicit formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using digital-analog blocks, combining the system's natural interaction with single-qubit gates.
result: They provide explicit decompositions and error bounds for Hamiltonian simulation, demonstrating the feasibility and efficiency of the digital-analog approach.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for implementing Hamiltonian simulation on digital-analog quantum processors, advancing the hybrid quantum systems paradigm.

title: Inverse Determination Of Light-matter Coupling In Disordered Systems From Transmittance Spectra

authors: Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, And Zlatko Papić
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, and Zlatko Papić

While nonstabilizerness (“magic”) is a key resource for universal quantum computation, its behavior in many-body quantum systems, especially near criticality, remains poorly understood. We develop a spectral transfer-matrix framework for the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Develops a spectral transfer-matrix framework to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy in infinite matrix product states, revealing signatures of nonstabilizerness near criticality.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness (magic) is essential for universal quantum computation, but its behavior in many-body systems, especially near critical points, is poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce a spectral transfer-matrix method to efficiently compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy for infinite matrix product states, enabling analysis of large systems.
result: They find that nonstabilizerness exhibits distinct signatures at critical points, such as scaling behavior and sensitivity to phase transitions.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool to study magic in many-body systems and suggests that criticality can enhance or modify nonstabilizerness, with implications for quantum computing resources.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical dynamical phases in kinetically constrained models using self-duality, connecting to non-equilibrium phase transitions.
motivation: To understand multicritical behavior in stochastic dynamics, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and phase transitions.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models and identify lines of self-duality separating dynamical phases.
result: They demonstrate the existence of multicritical points where multiple dynamical phases meet, protected by self-duality.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local and global quantum resources is fundamental for quantum information processing. This work aims to experimentally verify a theoretical bound on the sum of local coherence and quantum mutual information.
method: The authors prepare quantum states in a photonic setup and measure local coherence and quantum mutual information, comparing their sum to a theoretical upper bound.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming a local-global trade-off.
conclusion: The results establish a complementarity relation between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information tasks.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Optical probing of phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon-induced decoherence in SnV centers is crucial for their use as quantum emitters and spin-photon interfaces.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping measurements are performed on SnV centers in diamond to extract phonon coupling parameters.
result: The study reveals the phonon density of states and electron-phonon coupling strength, explaining temperature-dependent linewidth broadening.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the phononic environment of SnV centers, aiding the development of diamond-based quantum network nodes.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication requires accounting for relativistic effects that can degrade QKD performance; this work provides a systematic analysis of such frequency shifts.
method: The authors separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse, and gravitational contributions, and model their impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how these shifts affect key rates and provide bounds for practical satellite QKD implementations.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in satellite QKD system design, but can be mitigated with appropriate compensation techniques.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks to learn dissipative dynamics using contact variational principles.
motivation: Existing physics-informed ML methods handle dissipation via ad hoc modifications or require full-state information; a principled approach is needed.
method: Proposes a neural network architecture based on Herglotz variational principle and contact geometry to model nonconservative systems with dissipation.
result: Demonstrates accurate learning of dissipative dynamics (e.g., damped harmonic oscillator) without requiring full-state information or ad hoc dissipation terms.
conclusion: Contact variational principles provide a natural framework for learning dissipative systems, bridging machine learning and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables like work and heat in both jump and diffusion settings.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities in stochastic systems, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework based on phase separation and condensation, drawing analogies to neural networks and statistical physics.
result: They argue that condensates can implement classification, sensing, and decision-making via phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding living systems.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and Trotterization in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the electron temperature in mesoscopic metallic islands after a heating pulse, analyzing the relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: a fast initial relaxation due to electron-phonon coupling, followed by a slower process attributed to hyperfine interaction with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs thermalization in these systems, which has implications for quantum information devices operating at low temperatures.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its effectiveness on experimental data from semiconductor qubits.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit platforms, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence sources.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with qubit count, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating expressivity (via circuit complexity) to noise-induced variance suppression.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide quantitative estimates of the loss function variance as a function of noise strength and circuit depth.
conclusion: Noise, typically detrimental, can be beneficial for trainability in variational algorithms, offering a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise levels.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations to study string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects.
conclusion: The results provide new probes for string breaking and highlight the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Combines noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies with partial fault tolerance.
result: Achieves a molecular energy computation with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: This work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different approaches and aids in advancing simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can simplify certain gates and reduce resource overhead, motivating a survey of their roles.
method: The paper reviews theoretical embeddings of qudits into qubit systems, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates, reducing circuit depth and potentially improving fidelity, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, by leveraging higher-dimensional Hilbert spaces to simplify algorithms.

title: Fully Optimised Variational Simulation Of A Dynamical Quantum Phase Transition On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Lesley Gover, Vinul Wimalaweera, Fariha Azad, Matthew Decross, Michael Foss-Feig, And Andrew G. Green
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2109 (2026).

We time-evolve a translationally invariant quantum state on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion quantum processor, studying the dynamical quantum phase transition of the transverse field Ising model. This physics requires a delicate cancellation of phases in the many-body wavefunction and presents a tough challenge for current quantum devices. We follow the dynamics using a quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz, optimised for the time-evolution using a fidelity cost function. Sampling costs are mitigated by using the measured values of this circuit as stochastic corrections to a simple classical extrapolation of the ansatz parameters. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution and reveal a hitherto hidden simplicity of the evolution of the transverse-field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition.

.
tldr: This paper demonstrates variational quantum time-evolution on a trapped-ion quantum processor to study a dynamical quantum phase transition in the transverse field Ising model.
motivation: Dynamical quantum phase transitions are challenging to simulate on current quantum devices due to the need for delicate phase cancellations. The authors aim to show that variational quantum time-evolution can overcome these challenges.
method: They use a quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz optimized with a fidelity cost function, and mitigate sampling costs by using measured circuit values as stochastic corrections to a classical extrapolation of ansatz parameters.
result: The approach successfully follows the dynamics of the transverse field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition, revealing a hidden simplicity in the evolution.
conclusion: Variational quantum time-evolution is feasible on current trapped-ion quantum processors and can provide insights into complex quantum dynamics.

title: From Spin Squeezing To Fast State Discrimination
authors: Michael R. Geller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2108 (2026).

There is great interest in generating and controlling entanglement in Bose-Einstein condensates and similar ensembles for use in quantum computation, simulation, and sensing. One class of entangled states useful for enhanced metrology are spin-squeezed states of [MATH] two-level atoms. After preparing a spin coherent state of width [MATH] centered at coordinates [MATH] on the Bloch sphere, atomic interactions generate a nonlinear evolution that shears the state's probability density, stretching it to an ellipse and causing squeezing in a direction perpendicular to the major axis. Here we consider the same setup but in the [MATH] limit . This shrinks the initial coherent state to zero area. Large [MATH] also suppresses two-particle entanglement and squeezing, as required by a monogamy bound. The torsion (1-axis twist) is still present, however, and the center of the large [MATH] coherent state evolves as a qubit governed by a two-state Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The resulting nonlinearity is known to be a powerful resource in quantum computation. It can be used to implement single-input quantum state discrimination, an impossibility within linear one-particle quantum mechanics. We obtain a solution to the discrimination problem in terms of a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. We also consider an open-system variant containing both Bloch sphere torsion and dissipation. In this case it should be possible to generate two basins of attraction within the Bloch ball, having a shared boundary that can be used for a type of autonomous state discrimination. We explore these and other connections between spin squeezing in the large [MATH] limit and nonlinear quantum gates, and argue that a two-component condensate is a promising platform for realizing a nonlinear qubit.

.
tldr: Explores the connection between spin squeezing in the large-N limit and nonlinear quantum gates for state discrimination.
motivation: To understand how entanglement and nonlinearity in Bose-Einstein condensates can be harnessed for quantum computation and sensing.
method: Analytical study of the large-N limit of spin squeezing, mapping the dynamics to a nonlinear qubit via the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, and analyzing state discrimination using a Viviani curve.
result: Derives a solution for single-input quantum state discrimination using nonlinear evolution and identifies conditions for autonomous discrimination in open systems.
conclusion: Two-component condensates are a promising platform for realizing nonlinear qubits with applications in quantum state discrimination.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator localization and fragmentation in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and an entanglement bottleneck.
motivation: Understanding the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium quantum phases and their realizability on NISQ devices.
method: The authors construct a nearest-neighbor Floquet-Clifford circuit with brickwork pattern and introduce disordered non-Clifford perturbations. They analyze operator spreading, fragmentation into sectors, and compute the spectral form factor.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors with emergent local integrals of motion. The average operator spreading length is tunable, and initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across fragment boundaries. The spectral form factor shows a fragmentation time scale before random matrix theory behavior sets in.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, demonstrating that operator localization can persist under generic perturbations and lead to an entanglement bottleneck.

title: Phase-Sensitive Measurements On A Fermi–Hubbard Quantum Processor
authors: Alberto R. Cavallar, Luis Escalera-Moreno, Titus Franz, Timon Hilker, J. Ignacio Cirac, Philipp M. Preiss, And Benjamin F. Schiffer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2103 (2026).

Fermionic quantum processors are a promising platform for quantum simulation of correlated fermionic matter. In this work, we study a hardware-efficient protocol for measuring complex expectation values of the time-evolution operator, commonly referred to as Loschmidt echoes, with fermions in an optical superlattice. We analyze the algorithm for the Fermi–Hubbard model at half-filling as well as at finite doping. The method relies on global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution, the latter being realized by architecture-tailored pulse sequences starting from a product state of plaquettes. Our numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range. This allows one to measure spectral properties of the Fermi–Hubbard model, such as the local density of states, and paves the way for the study of finite-temperature properties in current fermionic quantum simulators.

.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient protocol for measuring Loschmidt echoes on a fermionic quantum processor to study spectral properties of the Fermi-Hubbard model.
motivation: Fermionic quantum processors are promising for simulating correlated fermionic matter, but measuring complex expectation values like Loschmidt echoes is challenging; this work aims to provide an efficient protocol.
method: The protocol uses global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution realized by architecture-tailored pulse sequences starting from a product state of plaquettes.
result: Numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range.
conclusion: The method enables measurement of spectral properties such as local density of states and paves the way for finite-temperature studies in current fermionic quantum simulators.

title: Polynomial Time Constructive Decision Algorithm For Multivariable Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Yuki Ito, Hitomi Mori, Kazuki Sakamoto, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2102 (2026).

Quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) have provided a unified framework for understanding many quantum algorithms, including factorization, matrix inversion, and Hamiltonian simulation. As a multivariable version of QSP, multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP) is proposed. M-QSP interleaves signal operators corresponding to each variable with signal processing operators, which provides an efficient means to perform multivariable polynomial transformations. However, the necessary and sufficient condition for what types of polynomials can be constructed by M-QSP is unknown. In this paper, we propose a classical algorithm to determine whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, which returns True or False. As one of the most important properties of this algorithm, its returning True is the necessary and sufficient condition. The proposed classical algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators. Our algorithm also provides a constructive method to select the necessary parameters for implementing M-QSP. These findings offer valuable insights for identifying practical applications of M-QSP.

.
tldr: A polynomial-time classical algorithm that decides whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, providing necessary and sufficient conditions.
motivation: M-QSP generalizes QSP to multiple variables, enabling efficient multivariable polynomial transformations, but the exact class of implementable polynomials was unknown, hindering practical applications.
method: The authors develop a classical algorithm based on algebraic conditions that checks implementability in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators, and also constructs the required parameters.
result: The algorithm returns True if and only if the polynomial pair is implementable, and runs in polynomial time, providing a constructive method for parameter selection.
conclusion: This work clarifies the expressibility of M-QSP and offers a practical tool for designing quantum algorithms that rely on multivariable polynomial transformations.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs over 21 km fiber.
motivation: Asymmetric HOM revival interference in QFCs had not been systematically investigated, and efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals was unreported.
method: Experimental setup with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, measuring HOM revivals across multiple time-bins, and distributing QFC over 21 km optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: Observed HOM revivals spanning up to 20 time-bins with visibilities around 70%, and distributed QFC over 21 km fiber with similar visibility.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Observation Of Phase Doubling And Entanglement In Coherent Matter-wave Reactions
authors: Shu Nagata, Tadej Mežnaršič, Chuixin Kong And Cheng Chin
abstract: Chemical reactions in a statistical ensemble are conventionally regarded as incoherent processes driven by thermodynamics. In the quantum degenerate regime, where atoms and molecules form coherent matter waves, reactions are theoretically described by nonlinear mixing of matter-wave fields. In this scenario, we expect phase matching between reactants and products, analogous to the mixing of photonic fields in nonlinear optics. Here we report on the observation of phase coherent reaction dynamics of Bose-condensed atoms and molecules near a Feshbach resonance. Using matter-wave diffraction with optical lattices, we verify spatial coherence of both atoms and molecules and observe phase doubling when atomic waves combine into molecular waves, the matter-wave analogue of optical frequency doubling. The diffraction patterns further reveal two-atom entanglement generated during the reaction. Our observations establish phase coherence and entanglement generation as two essential features of ‘quantum many-body chemistry’. Moreover, our work opens a pathway to control of reaction dynamics by manipulation of matter-wave phases.
tldr: Observation of phase coherence and entanglement in Bose-condensed atom-molecule reactions near a Feshbach resonance, demonstrating matter-wave nonlinear mixing analogous to nonlinear optics.
motivation: To explore quantum coherent reaction dynamics in degenerate quantum gases, where reactions are expected to exhibit phase matching and entanglement, moving beyond classical thermodynamics.
method: Using matter-wave diffraction with optical lattices to verify spatial coherence of atoms and molecules, and observing phase doubling in the diffraction patterns as atoms combine into molecules.
result: Phase doubling is observed, analogous to optical frequency doubling, and diffraction patterns reveal two-atom entanglement generated during the reaction.
conclusion: The work establishes phase coherence and entanglement as key features of quantum many-body chemistry, and opens pathways to control reaction dynamics via matter-wave phase manipulation.

title: Absence Of Poor Local Minima In Matrix Product States
authors: Hao-Kai Zhang, Chenghong Zhu, Shuo Liu, Shi-Xin Zhang, Tao Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum circuits suffer from severe trainability issues: even shallow circuits are swamped with poor local minima. Yet matrix product states (MPS), which can be prepared by sequential circuits, are remarkably trainable in practice -- as demonstrated by decades of successful density matrix renormalization group calculations. In this work, we resolve this apparent paradox by proving that the energy landscapes of MPS are free from poor local minima, under the same setting where brickwork circuits are not. The key insight is that the gauge freedom of MPS creates an effective local overparametrization that causes local minima to concentrate near the global minimum, analogous to overparametrized classical neural networks. We rigorously prove that the local minimum distribution of the MPS energy landscape is invariant under moves of the orthogonality center. Numerical experiments further confirm that the optimization of sequential circuits converges to near-optimal solutions even for random Hamiltonians, in stark contrast to brickwork circuits. Our findings highlight the pivotal role of effective local overparametrization in determining trainability, providing a valuable guide for overcoming the trainability bottleneck of variational quantum algorithms.

motivation: Quantum circuits suffer from poor local minima, but MPS are remarkably trainable; the paper resolves this paradox.
method: Theoretical proof using gauge freedom of MPS to show local minima distribution is invariant under orthogonality center moves, plus numerical experiments on random Hamiltonians.
result: MPS energy landscapes are free from poor local minima, unlike brickwork circuits; sequential circuits converge to near-optimal solutions.
conclusion: Effective local overparametrization from gauge freedom is key to trainability, guiding design of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Profiling A Rydberg-Atom Electric Field Sensor For Off-Resonant Detection Of Sub-100 MHz Rf Signals
authors: Michael A. Viray, Abby Halasi-Kun, Baran N. Kayim, Brian C. Sawyer, Robert Wyllie, David S. la Mantia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Rydberg-Atom electric field sensor optimized to detect signals at sub-100 MHz carrier frequencies. The sensing setup employs a sapphire vapor cell that allows for detection of signals below 100~MHz -- typical vapor cells made of glass or quartz demonstrate strong screening of radio frequency (RF) signals in this frequency regime. Applied signals are detected by observing AC Stark shifts in the atomic vapor energy levels. As a test case for the commercial utility of this receiver, we perform our tests at several carrier frequencies in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. At each carrier frequency, we report sensitivity, minimum detectable field, and detectable electric-field dynamic range. We also present a routine for optimizing off-resonant signal detection by tuning experimental parameters such as Rydberg coupler laser detuning and RF local oscillator strength. This Python-based optimization routine, which can be used at any off-resonant carrier frequency, is shared on Github for others to use in their own investigations.
tldr: This paper presents a Rydberg-atom electric field sensor optimized for sub-100 MHz RF signals using a sapphire vapor cell and an off-resonant detection scheme.
motivation: Standard glass or quartz vapor cells screen low-frequency RF signals, limiting Rydberg-atom sensors to higher frequencies. The authors aim to extend sensitivity to the sub-100 MHz range for applications like ISM band detection.
method: A sapphire vapor cell is used to reduce RF screening. AC Stark shifts in Rydberg atoms are measured to detect off-resonant signals. A Python-based optimization routine tunes experimental parameters (coupler laser detuning, local oscillator strength) for optimal sensitivity.
result: The sensor achieves sensitivity, minimum detectable field, and dynamic range at several ISM band carrier frequencies below 100 MHz. The optimization routine improves off-resonant detection performance.
conclusion: The sapphire cell enables Rydberg-atom sensing at sub-100 MHz, and the optimization routine provides a practical tool for adapting the sensor to different frequencies.

title: Trainability Of Iqp Quantum Circuit Born Machines Under Gaussian Initialization
authors: Gennaro de Luca
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Circuit Born Machines (QCBMs) offer a natural approach to generative machine learning by leveraging the Born rule. Recent work has provided a method to classically train QCBMs with Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) circuits via the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) loss. Despite the assumed intractability of sampling from IQP circuits classically, their expectation values can be computed classically, enabling training of these IQP QCBMs. However, quantum machine learning (QML) models have various other challenges, including trainability issues caused by exponential concentration or barren plateaus. While these issues have been explored for parameters sampled from a uniform distribution, little work has been done to rigorously treat the use of arbitrary Gaussian initialization schemes. This work leverages Stein's lemma and Lipschitz concentration bounds for Gaussian random variables to provide an analytical lower bound of the variance of the gradient and a probabilistic concentration bound of the deviation of the gradient from its mean. It discusses strategies to either avoid or encourage exponential concentration, as well as the conditions under which barren plateaus are more likely to occur.
tldr: Analyzes trainability of IQP quantum circuit Born machines under Gaussian initialization, providing gradient variance bounds and concentration results.
motivation: Quantum machine learning models often suffer from barren plateaus, but little is known about Gaussian initialization schemes; this work aims to fill that gap.
method: Uses Stein's lemma and Lipschitz concentration bounds for Gaussian random variables to derive analytical lower bounds on gradient variance and probabilistic concentration bounds.
result: Provides conditions under which exponential concentration (barren plateaus) occurs or can be avoided for IQP QCBMs with Gaussian initialization.
conclusion: Gaussian initialization can either mitigate or exacerbate trainability issues depending on parameter choices, offering guidance for practical QML training.

The work extends previous analyses that considered uniform parameter distributions to arbitrary Gaussian initializations, offering a more rigorous treatment of initialization effects in quantum machine learning.

title: Experimental Implementation Of Continuous-variable Qaoa On A Quad-rail Lattice Cluster State
authors: Shota Yokoyama, Atsushi Sakaguchi, Jun-Ichi Yoshikawa, Hironari Nagayoshi, Warit Asavanant, Kan Takase, Takuji Hiraoka, Akira Furusawa, Hidehiro Yonezawa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the continuous-variable quantum approximate optimization algorithm (CV-QAOA) for multi-variable problems and multiple QAOA depths using a measurement-based CV quantum computing platform on a quad-rail lattice (QRL) cluster state. We propose a systematic method to map arbitrary quadratic cost functions onto the QRL architecture and examine the resulting construction in settings involving up to 100 modes. Using the programmable platform, we prepare the CV-QAOA ansatz and optimize the variational parameters via Bayesian optimization. We then investigate the performance on quadratic optimization problems and observe that increasing the depth from 1 to 2 improves performance, whereas further increases yield only limited gains. In contrast, numerical simulations under idealized conditions, assuming an infinite number of measurement shots and gradient-based optimization, indicate that the performance of CV-QAOA can improve with increasing depth, suggesting that the experimentally observed limitations primarily arise from noise accumulation and classical optimization challenges. This work provides an experimental demonstration of CV-QAOA on a programmable CV platform and establishes a foundation for future developments of variational quantum algorithms in CV systems.

conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle experimental demonstration of CV-QAOA and highlights noise as a key limitation for deeper circuits.
