title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of spin and valley dynamics in a monolayer semiconductor using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect, achieving subpicosecond manipulation.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information processing in van der Waals heterostructures.
method: The authors use femtosecond optical pulses to excite and probe spin and valley coherence in a monolayer WSe2 on a ferromagnetic substrate, exploiting the magnetic proximity effect.
result: They observe subpicosecond coherent oscillations of the valley polarization and spin polarization, with control over the phase and amplitude via the magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The anomalous magnetic proximity effect enables ultrafast coherent control of spin and valley degrees of freedom, offering a pathway for valleytronic quantum devices.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan

The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity in α-RuCl3, attributed to chiral Majorana edge modes, but the focus is on condensed matter physics of topological phases rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To confirm the existence of non-Abelian anyons via chiral edge modes in a Kitaev candidate material, addressing reproducibility issues of quantized thermal Hall effect.
method: Geometric engineering of the thermal Hall effect in α-RuCl3 single crystals, measuring thermal Hall conductivity as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: Observation of half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity consistent with chiral Majorana edge modes, with improved reproducibility through sample engineering.
conclusion: The results provide strong evidence for non-Abelian anyons in α-RuCl3, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter physics experiment with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Loss-resistant Bright-seeded Su(1,1) Quantum Interferometer Based On Joint Detection
authors: Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

A quantum interferometer can achieve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit by using the nonclassical properties of the quantum state. The SU(1,1) interferometer, a commonly used quantum interferometer, can be realized by replacing the linear beam splitters in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer wit…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063712] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A loss-resistant SU(1,1) quantum interferometer using bright-seeded joint detection to enhance phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit.
motivation: To overcome the sensitivity degradation due to internal losses in SU(1,1) interferometers, which limits their practical quantum-enhanced metrology performance.
method: The authors propose a bright-seeded SU(1,1) interferometer with joint detection, theoretically analyzing its phase sensitivity under loss using a quantum optics model.
result: The scheme achieves phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit even with significant internal losses, demonstrating loss resistance.
conclusion: The bright-seeded joint detection approach provides a practical way to realize robust quantum-enhanced interferometry.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, and Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition between Floquet and Bloch topological regimes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations, and quasienergy band analysis reveals topological transitions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch topological modes, contributing to the understanding of topological photonics.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical techniques for laser cooling are inefficient for large crystals.
method: The authors develop and apply optimized numerical methods to simulate Doppler laser cooling of 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: They identify optimal cooling parameters that reduce cooling time and improve final temperature, enhancing the performance of quantum sensing protocols.
conclusion: Optimized Doppler cooling protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals for high-sensitivity quantum sensing.

title: Rabi Oscillations With Close-range Quantum Vortex States
authors: Sam Patrick
abstract:
Author(s): Sam Patrick

Quantum vortices separated by distances much larger than their core size interact via their long-range velocity field. At smaller separations, however, the influence of the core's compressibility strongly influences the vortex dynamics. Using the example of a compact necklace of five vortices, it is…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063309] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Rabi oscillations of quantum vortices in a Bose-Einstein condensate at close range, focusing on core compressibility effects.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics at small separations is important for quantum turbulence and superfluid hydrodynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use a compact necklace of five vortices and analyze their dynamics via numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
result: They find that core compressibility significantly alters the Rabi oscillation frequency and damping compared to point-vortex models.
conclusion: Close-range vortex interactions require models that account for core structure, but the work remains within condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Robust Quantum Control For Bragg Pulse Design In Atom Interferometry
authors: Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, And Malcolm G. Boshier
abstract:
Author(s): Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, and Malcolm G. Boshier

We formulate a robust optimal control algorithm to synthesize minimum-energy pulses that can transfer a cold atom system into various momentum states. The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iterate the control towards a minimum-ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063305] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A robust optimal control algorithm for designing Bragg pulses in atom interferometry, focusing on momentum state transfer.
motivation: To improve the robustness and efficiency of Bragg pulse design for cold atom interferometry, which is sensitive to experimental imperfections.
method: Uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iteratively find minimum-energy control pulses.
result: Demonstrates robust pulse designs that achieve high-fidelity momentum state transfer under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm provides a systematic way to design robust quantum control pulses for atom interferometry applications.

title: Topological Routing In Chern Insulators
authors: Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, And Sean D. Nixon
abstract:
Author(s): Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, and Sean D. Nixon

Chern insulator systems are realizable in numerous physical systems and can support robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy. A routing functionality constructed from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions, using coupled Haldane-type systems is proposed. By adjusting the strength of a magnet…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063510] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a topological routing scheme in Chern insulators using coupled Haldane-type systems for robust nonreciprocal energy transmission.
motivation: To achieve robust routing of energy in photonic or electronic systems by exploiting topological properties of Chern insulators.
method: The authors design a routing structure from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions and adjust the strength of a magnet to control the routing.
result: The system supports robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy, enabling topological routing.
conclusion: Topological routing in Chern insulators is feasible and may have applications in robust energy transport.

title: Intrinsic Quasiparticle Lifetime In Superconducting Aluminum
authors: K. Norowski, M. Foltyn, A. Savin, And M. Zgirski
abstract:
Author(s): K. Norowski, M. Foltyn, A. Savin, and M. Zgirski

We use time-resolved thermometry to monitor the decay of nonequilibrium quasiparticles in superconducting Al in the temperature range from [MATH] to [MATH]. The quasiparticle lifetime at higher temperatures ([MATH]) agrees well …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214512] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Measures quasiparticle lifetime in superconducting aluminum using time-resolved thermometry.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics is important for superconducting qubit coherence, but the paper focuses on material properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved thermometry to monitor decay of nonequilibrium quasiparticles in Al films.
result: Quasiparticle lifetime agrees with theory at higher temperatures but deviates at lower temperatures.
conclusion: Provides experimental data on quasiparticle lifetime, relevant for superconducting device engineering but not directly advancing the user's research directions.

title: Generation Of Chirality And Orbital Magnetization By Stone-Wales-type Lattice Defects In The Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

In this work we extend our study of the effect of certain crystallographic defects on the spin-1/2 Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, focusing on its gapless phase and contrasting with the gapped phase. We identify a Stone-Wales (SW) local defect consisting of a [MATH] bond rotation that preserves Ki…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224419] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales lattice defects on the Kitaev spin liquid, focusing on chirality and orbital magnetization.
motivation: Understanding how crystallographic defects affect the properties of quantum spin liquids is important for characterizing real materials.
method: The authors analyze the Kitaev honeycomb model with Stone-Wales defects using analytical and numerical methods, examining both gapless and gapped phases.
result: They find that Stone-Wales defects generate chirality and orbital magnetization in the Kitaev spin liquid.
conclusion: Lattice defects can induce topological and magnetic responses in Kitaev materials, which may be observable experimentally.

title: Theory Of Relaxation And Its Effects On The Electronic Structure In Twisted Systems
authors: Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, and Cheng-Cheng Liu

Here, the authors present an analytical and physically transparent theory of lattice relaxation in twisted systems. They show how the balance between intralayer elasticity and interlayer adhesion determines the relaxation pattern, and how this pattern can be analytically embedded into moiré electronic Hamiltonians. The work reveals how relaxation reshapes flat bands and shifts topological transitions toward experimentally relevant twist angles.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An analytical theory of lattice relaxation in twisted 2D materials and its effect on electronic structure.
motivation: To understand how lattice relaxation reshapes moiré flat bands and topological transitions in twisted systems.
method: Analytical modeling balancing intralayer elasticity and interlayer adhesion, embedded into moiré electronic Hamiltonians.
result: Reveals how relaxation shifts flat bands and topological transitions toward experimentally relevant twist angles.
conclusion: Provides a physically transparent framework for incorporating relaxation effects into moiré band structure calculations.

title: Bosonic Holes In Quadratic Bosonic Systems
authors: Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Hole degrees of freedom play a central role in the exact solution of quadratic (mean-field) systems. Although a variety of experiments have suggested the existence of bosonic holes, a consistent and complete theory has long been hindered by the ghost problems. Here, we resolve the ghost problem and …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224305] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves the ghost problem in quadratic bosonic systems and develops a consistent theory of bosonic holes.
motivation: Bosonic holes have been suggested by experiments but lacked a consistent theory due to ghost problems.
method: The authors resolve the ghost problem and provide a complete theoretical framework for bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.
result: A consistent and complete theory of bosonic holes is established, resolving the long-standing ghost problem.
conclusion: The work provides a solid theoretical foundation for understanding bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.

title: Topological Phase Transitions In Twisted Bilayer graphene/hBN From Interlayer Coupling And Substrate Potentials
authors: Huiwen Wang And Wei Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Huiwen Wang and Wei Jiang

Twisted bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride (TBG/hBN) hosts rich topological and correlated quantum phases, such as (fractional) Chern insulators, whose character is dictated by the topology of the moiré flat band. This topology is highly sensitive to several material parameters in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235109] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN, focusing on the effect of interlayer coupling and substrate potentials on moiré flat band topology.
motivation: Understanding how material parameters control the topology of moiré flat bands is crucial for engineering correlated and topological phases in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN systems.
method: The authors use a continuum model to compute the band structure and topological invariants (Chern numbers) as a function of interlayer coupling strength and substrate potential parameters.
result: They identify phase transitions between Chern insulator phases and trivial phases, mapping out phase diagrams that show how topology depends on the interplay of coupling and substrate.
conclusion: The topology of moiré flat bands in TBG/hBN can be tuned via interlayer coupling and substrate potentials, providing a route to control quantum phases in these systems.

title: Real-space Decay Of Flat-band Projectors From Compact Localized States
authors: Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, And Alexei Andreanov
abstract:
Author(s): Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, and Alexei Andreanov

Flat bands (FBs) with compact localized eigenstates (CLSs) fall into three main categories, controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set: orthogonal, linearly independent, and linearly dependent (singular). A CLS parametrization allows us to continuously tune a linearly independent FB into …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235110] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the real-space decay of flat-band projectors from compact localized states in flat-band systems.
motivation: Understanding the algebraic properties of compact localized states (CLS) and their projectors is important for characterizing flat-band systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors classify flat bands into three categories based on CLS properties and analyze the decay of projectors using a CLS parametrization.
result: They show that the decay of projectors is controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set, with singular CLS leading to slower decay.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of flat-band projectors but remains within condensed matter physics without clear relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Strange Metal Behavior In A Toy Model With Selective Mottness
authors: M. S. Laad And S. R. Hassan
abstract:
Author(s): M. S. Laad and S. R. Hassan

The interplay between band and atomic aspects in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states, or wide-band and effectively dispersionless electronic states is increasingly expected to lead to novel behavior. Using dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), we investigate strange metal-like beh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235111] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses DMFT to study strange metal behavior in a toy model with coexisting wide and flat bands, focusing on selective Mottness.
motivation: Strange metal behavior in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states is not well understood; the authors aim to model this using a toy model.
method: Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) is applied to a toy model with selective Mottness to investigate strange metal-like behavior.
result: The model reproduces strange metal characteristics such as linear-in-temperature resistivity and non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: Selective Mottness in a toy model can capture key features of strange metal behavior, providing insights into correlated electron systems.

title: Accurate Computation Of The Energy Variance For Ground States And $〈〈{\mathcal{L}}^{†}\mathcal{L}〉〉$ For Steady States Using iPEPS
authors: Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, And Philippe Corboz
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, and Philippe Corboz

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) provide a powerful tensor network ansatz for two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit. In this paper, we introduce an approach to accurately compute the energy variance of an iPEPS, enabling systematic extrapolations of the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245114] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to compute energy variance for ground states and steady states using infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) for 2D quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Accurate computation of energy variance is important for systematic extrapolations of ground state energies and for studying steady states of open quantum systems, but existing iPEPS methods lack precision.
method: The authors develop an approach to compute the energy variance of an iPEPS by contracting appropriate tensor networks, and also extend it to compute the expectation value of L†L for steady states of Lindblad master equations.
result: The method yields accurate energy variances for ground states and steady states, enabling reliable extrapolations and improved characterization of iPEPS approximations.
conclusion: The proposed technique enhances the utility of iPEPS for studying 2D quantum systems, particularly for assessing the quality of ground state approximations and for open system steady states.

title: Environment-matrix-product Operator For Boundary-free Large-scale Quantum Many-body Simulations
authors: Souta Shimozono And Chisa Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Souta Shimozono and Chisa Hotta

We propose an alternative to the infinite density-matrix renormalization approach for accessing quantum many-body states within a finite-size calculation that faithfully mimics the thermodynamic limit. Our method constructs environment-matrix-product operators (environment-MPOs) representing the Ham…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an environment-matrix-product operator method for boundary-free large-scale quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: To simulate quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit without finite-size effects, overcoming limitations of infinite DMRG.
method: Constructs environment-MPOs representing the Hamiltonian of a finite-size system that mimics the thermodynamic limit, using a boundary-free approach.
result: The method enables accurate simulation of large-scale quantum many-body systems with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The environment-MPO approach is a viable alternative to infinite DMRG for boundary-free simulations.

title: Update Of Hartree-Fock Theory For Hubbard-like Models
authors: E. Langmann And J. Lenells
abstract:
Author(s): E. Langmann and J. Lenells

We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitative errors in established condensed matter results.
motivation: Standard Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard models yields incorrect results; the authors aim to provide a corrected formulation.
method: The authors revisit and update the restricted Hartree-Fock formalism for Fermi Hubbard-like models, deriving corrected mean-field equations.
result: They show that previous textbook results are qualitatively wrong and present corrected solutions.
conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard treatment for Hubbard-like models in condensed matter physics.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond extended and localized states, specifically the emergence of multiple critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, using numerical methods to characterize phase transitions.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals new reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They show that the system can host topological phases and gauge-invariant dynamics, with potential for observing anyonic excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental platform for simulating topological gauge theories and studying their properties.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms
authors: Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, and Oded Zilberberg

The Kondo effect is a paradigmatic model of strongly correlated physics, where a magnetic impurity forms a many-body singlet with a fermionic environment. The properties of this singlet depend sensitively on correlations within the environment, which are particularly pronounced in one dimension, whe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023244] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo physics in one-dimensional quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with manifestations in ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, especially with a repulsive impurity.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo singlet formation and its properties in quantum wires.
result: They find that the repulsive impurity leads to distinct Kondo signatures that can be observed in ytterbium atom experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to realize and detect Kondo physics in quantum wires with repulsive impurities.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, and Markus Heyl

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A new neural network architecture combining convolutional and transformer layers for representing quantum wave functions, achieving high accuracy on frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Improve variational wave function representations for quantum many-body systems, especially those with strong frustration or time-dependent behavior.
method: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function that respects lattice symmetries and uses attention mechanisms to capture long-range correlations.
result: Sets new accuracy benchmarks for ground states of frustrated magnets and for simulating quantum dynamics.
conclusion: The architecture is a powerful tool for quantum many-body problems, but the paper focuses on computational methods rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts
abstract:
Author(s): Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, and Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic techniques for gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS), focusing on gauge fixing and translation invariance in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative phenomena but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods offer an alternative, but handling gauge symmetry and translation invariance algorithmically is challenging.
method: The authors propose algorithms for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in Gaussian fermionic PEPS, leveraging the structure of Gaussian states to efficiently represent and manipulate gauge-invariant states.
result: They demonstrate that their gauge fixing and translation invariance algorithms work effectively for small systems, enabling the construction of translation-invariant gauge-invariant PEPS.
conclusion: The work provides algorithmic tools for simulating lattice gauge theories with tensor networks, but the focus is on computational methods rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy to quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework to simplify the problem.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and relates this to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality connects to exactly solvable dynamics and quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit models.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior, but the field is still developing; further research is needed for quantum applications.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement using spin-squeezed states in lossy atom interferometers, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but is degraded by losses and temperature.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses, and one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite realistic losses.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic conditions, but finite temperature remains a significant challenge.

title: Hidden Time-nonlocal Floquet Symmetries
authors: Sigmund Kohler And Jesús Casado-Pascual
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2112 (2026).

We investigate the Floquet spectrum of a detuned, driven two-level system and show that it exhibits exact quasienergy crossings when the detuning is an integer multiple of the energy quantum of the driving field. This behavior can be explained by a hidden time-nonlocal parity, which allows the Floquet modes to be classified as even or odd. Then a generic feature is the emergence of exact crossings between quasienergies of different parity. A constructive proof of the existence of the symmetry is based on a scalar recurrence relation. Moreover, we present a general scheme for its numerical computation, which can be applied to models beyond the two-level system. Analytical results are illustrated with numerical data.

.
tldr: The paper studies hidden time-nonlocal Floquet symmetries in driven two-level systems, explaining exact quasienergy crossings via a parity classification.
motivation: To understand the origin of exact quasienergy crossings in detuned driven two-level systems, which are not explained by standard Floquet theory.
method: Analytical derivation using a scalar recurrence relation and numerical computation of the symmetry operator for models beyond two-level systems.
result: Exact quasienergy crossings occur when detuning is an integer multiple of the driving quantum; these are classified by a hidden time-nonlocal parity symmetry.
conclusion: The discovered symmetry provides a general framework for understanding level crossings in Floquet systems, with potential applications in quantum control.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving QUBO problems using a circuit that mimics imaginary time evolution.
motivation: QUBO problems are important for combinatorial optimization, and near-term quantum devices may offer advantages if algorithms can be designed to work with limited resources.
method: The algorithm optimizes a parameterized quantum circuit to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values to avoid full energy evaluation, and iteratively updates the initial state.
result: Classical simulations achieve high approximation ratios for up to 150 qubits, and hardware runs on IBM devices for 40, 60, and 80 qubits yield solutions comparable to simulated annealing.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm is a practical approach for QUBO on near-term quantum computers, with linear entanglement scaling suggesting classical hardness.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo For Fractional Quantum Hall States
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We develop a hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method to efficiently compute the physical observables from the samplings of the Laughlin and the Moore–Read (MR) wave functions of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems. With the advancements in methodology, including global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, our HMC simulation is significantly faster than the widely used Metropolis Monte Carlo scheme. As a result, we can readily simulate systems with electron numbers on both disk and sphere geometries. We apply this method to investigate the topological shift obtained from the edge dipole moment, computed from the wave function density on the disk. We also numerically computed the non-Abelian braiding matrices for different braiding schemes of the MR quasiholes on the sphere. Results with much better quality compared with previous works have been achieved. With the thermodynamic limit results obtained at ease, we also discuss the future usage of our method to clarify the questions on the instability of FQH states in an ideal Chern band setting or under quantum decoherence.
tldr: Develops a hybrid Monte Carlo method for simulating fractional quantum Hall wave functions, focusing on computational efficiency and topological properties.
motivation: Efficient simulation of Laughlin and Moore-Read states is needed to study topological shifts and non-Abelian braiding in fractional quantum Hall systems.
method: Uses hybrid Monte Carlo with global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry to sample wave functions faster than Metropolis.
result: Achieves significantly faster simulations for systems on disk and sphere, computes topological shift and non-Abelian braiding matrices with improved quality.
conclusion: The method enables thermodynamic limit studies and can be extended to investigate FQH state instability in Chern bands or under decoherence.

title: Wave Packets From The Spectrum
authors: Chunjun Cao, Oliver Friedrich, Marin Girard, Nicolas Loizeau, Ashmeet Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The freedom to change Fock basis seems to ensure a minimum amount of locality in lattice theories in the following sense: If [MATH] for [MATH] is a lattice of creation and annihilation operators and if a given Hamiltonian [MATH] induces highly non-local dynamics on that lattice, then it will usually be possible to change to a new set of operators [MATH] in terms of which the dynamics appear less non-local. We demonstrate this by turning a highly non-local random matrix model into a local, 1D lattice theory where particles can propagate in localized wave packets. More generally, we show that any Hamiltonian can be made to look like such a theory, with the lattice dispersion relation and the non-integrability of the theory depending on the spectrum of [MATH]. We argue that our results are a step towards quantum mereology for fields.
tldr: The paper shows that any Hamiltonian can be transformed into a local 1D lattice theory with wave packet propagation by changing the Fock basis, using the spectrum to define locality.
motivation: To understand how locality emerges in quantum field theories and to develop a quantum mereology for fields.
method: The authors demonstrate that by choosing a new set of creation/annihilation operators based on the Hamiltonian's spectrum, a highly non-local random matrix model becomes a local 1D lattice theory with wave packets.
result: Any Hamiltonian can be made to appear as a local lattice theory with a dispersion relation and non-integrability determined by its spectrum.
conclusion: This work is a step towards quantum mereology, suggesting that locality is not fundamental but can be derived from the spectrum.

title: Identical Bosons, Large Occupation Numbers And Classical Field Description
authors: Gaurav Goswami
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a system with a large number of identical Bosons, it is common to claim, often without any additional justifications, that, when the mean occupation number in a single particle state is sufficiently large, classical field description will be applicable. This is why e.g. for ultra-light dark matter, the classical field equations are used to compute its dynamics. In this work, we test the validity and robustness of this assumption based on the criterion [MATH] for classical field behaviour and applying it to aribtrary quantum states. We find that an arbitrary state with large occupation number doesn't behave classically while imposing some restrictions on the state vectors can improve the classical behavior. Since coherent states are known to have quasi-classical behaviour, we also ask how much deviation from coherent state can spoil the classical behaviour. Based on this analysis, we find that it is the proximity of the state to a large occupation coherent state rather than large occupation number itself which ensures validity of classical description. Implications of this for ultra light dark matter are discussed.
tldr: The paper investigates when a large-occupation-number bosonic system can be described by classical fields, finding that proximity to a coherent state is key, not just large occupation.
motivation: Ultra-light dark matter is often modeled using classical field equations, but the validity of this approximation for arbitrary quantum states with large occupation numbers is not well justified.
method: The author uses a criterion for classical field behavior and applies it to arbitrary quantum states, analyzing deviations from coherent states.
result: An arbitrary state with large occupation number does not behave classically; classical behavior requires the state to be close to a large-occupation coherent state.
conclusion: The classical field description for ultra-light dark matter is valid only when the quantum state is near a coherent state, not merely when occupation numbers are large.

title: Effective Training Principles Of Physical Reservoirs
authors: Sobhi Saeed, Mehmet M\"uft\"uoglu, Glitta R. Cheeran, Juliane Heim, Bennet Fischer, Mario Chemnitz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reservoir computers benefit from the inherent complexity of optical phenomena, which provide rich, often nonlinear dynamics. However, training directly on the reservoir's output renders the system prone to overfitting and computationally inefficient during the training phase. In this work, we investigate strategies to mitigate overfitting and reduce computational overhead through output pruning and regularization. We compare loss-minimizing search methods (Equal Search and Branch and Bound) against an output-oriented statistical filtering approach (Variance Filter) and random pruning, highlighting advantages and disadvantages of each approach and the overall importance of informed reservoir output sampling, particularly for a shrinking latent space. We further demonstrate that enforcing readout selection across the full output spectrum improves performance, especially for non-iterative methods. Additionally, we examine L1 and L2 regularization techniques (LASSO and ridge regression), both of which significantly enhance performance on highly nonlinear tasks such as the Spiral Benchmark. While our methods are of general use, results are obtained from and discussed exemplarily for a nonlinear fiber-optical extreme learning machine. Overall, this study provides a deep analysis of the reservoirs' hidden-layer filtering mechanisms and the output-layer training, enabling optimized performance in physical reservoir computing systems.
tldr: This paper studies training strategies for physical reservoir computers, focusing on overfitting mitigation and computational efficiency.
motivation: Reservoir computers suffer from overfitting and high computational cost during training; the authors aim to improve performance through output pruning and regularization.
method: They compare loss-minimizing search methods (Equal Search, Branch and Bound) with statistical filtering (Variance Filter) and random pruning, and examine L1/L2 regularization (LASSO, ridge regression) on a nonlinear fiber-optical extreme learning machine.
result: Informed output sampling across the full spectrum improves performance, and regularization significantly enhances accuracy on highly nonlinear tasks.
conclusion: The study provides guidelines for optimizing physical reservoir computing systems by careful output selection and regularization.

title: Towards The Implementation Of A Quantum Classifier
authors: Lorenzo Confalonieri, Adri\'an P\'erez Salinas, Stefano Carrazza
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the use of a quantum circuit as a binary classification model in the context of quantum machine learning. We call this model, binary quantum classifier. First, we describe fundamental concepts of quantum computing and introduce the computational tool used: Qibo, an open-source framework for efficient quantum simulations and quantum hardware control. Then, we describe how to design a binary quantum classifier for the classification of images and small arrays of variables by showing how to input data in the circuit, defining a quantum circuit model Ansatz with trainable parameters and a loss function, and implementing multiple minimizers. We test our quantum classifier with two data sets. The first one is the MNIST data set which is composed of handwritten digits (reduced to only handwritten zeros and handwritten ones for binary classification). We study the behavior of different minimizers by increasing the number of layers of the Ansatz. The second data set represents two different high energy collisions that can occur at colliders such as LHC (CERN). Due to in-time proton-proton interactions known as pile-up, we distinguish two different data sets: "without pile-up" and "with pile-up". These collisions can be represented by images of size 32x32 or by six high-level variables that we call features. By increasing the size of the training data set and the number of layers of the Ansatz, we search for the best minimizer. Splitting the data set in training set and test set, we compute: ROC curve, AUC score, confusion matrices and test set accuracy. For "with pile-up" images, we compare the results obtained with the quantum classifier with a small convolutional neural network. We conclude that is possible to build a binary quantum classifier with a quantum circuit and we highlight its performances and limitations in comparison with classical technologies.
tldr: This paper implements a binary quantum classifier using Qibo for image and high-energy physics data, comparing performance to classical neural networks.
motivation: To explore the feasibility and performance of quantum machine learning for classification tasks, particularly in high-energy physics.
method: Designs a variational quantum circuit ansatz with trainable parameters, uses Qibo for simulation, and trains on MNIST and LHC collision data with various optimizers.
result: The quantum classifier achieves reasonable accuracy on both datasets, but performance is limited compared to a small convolutional neural network, especially with pile-up data.
conclusion: Quantum classifiers can be built and trained, but current performance and scalability are not competitive with classical methods for these tasks.

title: Unidirectional-like Edge Transport Induced By Non-Hermitian Skin Effects
authors: Junyi Rao, Jinting Ding, Qinghua Guo, Jun He, Xiang Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Hermitian skin effects (NHSEs) enable dramatic boundary accumulation of waves, yet their experimental realization typically demands engineered nonreciprocity or spatially patterned loss. Here we demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that uniform loss provides a simple and previously overlooked mechanism for enforcing unidirectional-like edge transport in photonic crystals (PhCs) that breaks time-reversal symmetry in the presence of nonchiral edge states. Using a core cladding geometry where domains share identical Chern numbers but possess distinct bulk polarizations, we show that uniform loss activates NHSEs that reshape the spectral topology of edge bands, giving rise to point gap windings that dictate a one way propagation. Near field measurements confirm that loss converts intrinsically bidirectional interface states into a unidirectional-like circulation around the entire domain wall, showing excellent agreement with theory. Our results establish uniform loss as a universal and structurally simple route for achieving unidirectional-like wave transport.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that uniform loss in photonic crystals can induce unidirectional-like edge transport via non-Hermitian skin effects.
motivation: Non-Hermitian skin effects typically require engineered nonreciprocity or patterned loss; the authors seek a simpler mechanism using uniform loss to achieve unidirectional wave transport.
method: They design a photonic crystal with a core-cladding geometry where domains share identical Chern numbers but distinct bulk polarizations, and apply uniform loss to activate NHSEs that reshape edge band topology.
result: Near-field measurements confirm that loss converts bidirectional interface states into unidirectional-like circulation around the domain wall, matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Uniform loss provides a universal and structurally simple route for achieving unidirectional-like wave transport in photonic systems.

title: Analytical Performance Evaluation Of Quantum Radar Architectures: From Single-photon To Entangled-noise Radars
authors: Ali Motazedifard Hossein Allahverdi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of two classes of quantum radars, including quantum direct-detection and quantum-entangled noise radars. In the first case, inspired by the well-established concept of single-photon LiDARs, we investigated the performance of single-photon radars, in which state-of-the-art single microwave-photon detectors are employed to enhance the detection sensitivity and enable the detection of weaker signals. We derived analytical expressions for the maximum detection range of both classes of quantum radars in terms of the Lambert W function, by considering all relevant system, target, and environmental parameters. Our formulation facilitates direct comparison of noise radars with direct-detection radars and suggests that a quantum-entangled noise radar can be regarded as an enhanced direct-detection radar with an effective threshold signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, we applied this framework to classical-correlated noise radars and defined the parameter range enhancement factor (REF) to quantify the superiority of quantum-entangled noise radars over their classical counterparts. Moreover, we introduced a rule-of-thumb for approximating the REF. We also examined the influence of limitations imposed by various microwave detection technologies. Our analysis shows that the conventional antennas limit the potential benefits of quantum-entangled noise radar systems. We also demonstrated that the optimal detection method for these radars is a microwave detector based on a quantum transducer combined with a single optical-photon detector. We showed that, with the current technology, implementing a quantum-entangled noise radar with the maximum detection range on the order of few kilometers is possible. Finally, we explored the potential applications of quantum-entangled noise radars.
tldr: This paper analytically evaluates the performance of quantum radar architectures, focusing on single-photon and entangled-noise radars, deriving maximum detection ranges and comparing them to classical counterparts.
motivation: Quantum radar is a sensing application that may offer advantages over classical radar, but its practical performance limits need to be understood.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for maximum detection range using the Lambert W function, considering system, target, and environmental parameters, and compare direct-detection and entangled-noise radars.
result: Quantum-entangled noise radars can be seen as enhanced direct-detection radars with an effective threshold SNR; current technology allows detection ranges on the order of a few kilometers.
conclusion: Quantum radar performance is limited by conventional antennas, and optimal detection requires a quantum transducer combined with a single optical-photon detector.

title: Support Sufficiency As Action-sufficient Compression: A Single-cycle Rate-regret Formulation
authors: Mark Walsh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robust decision-making requires compression. A system that forms a rich support state cannot usually preserve its full structure at the point of action. It must retain only those distinctions needed to act, verify, abstain, or defer under the current consequence geometry. This paper formalizes support sufficiency as action-sufficient compression. Let [MATH] denote a full support state, [MATH] a finite action set, and [MATH] a consequence geometry specifying payoff structure. For fixed [MATH], the coarsest exactly action-sufficient compression is the quotient of support space by policy equivalence. Two support states may be merged exactly when they require the same optimal action. This clarifies why content-only and scalar-confidence-only arbitration fail whenever their induced partitions cross action boundaries. Approximate sufficiency is then defined by bounded expected policy regret. In the finite single-cycle setting, this yields a rate-regret problem with source [MATH], reproduction alphabet [MATH], and distortion given by consequence-sensitive regret. The optimal stochastic action channel inherits the standard rate-distortion Gibbs form, applied here to support states with regret distortion. The contribution is interpretive: action adequacy is distinguished from reconstruction fidelity, information-bottleneck prediction, and rational inattention. Robust single-cycle arbitration does not require preserving all support, but it does require preserving the distinctions that consequence geometry makes action-relevant.
tldr: This paper formalizes support sufficiency as action-sufficient compression using a rate-regret formulation, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Robust decision-making requires compression of support states to action-relevant distinctions, but existing methods like content-only or confidence-only arbitration fail when they cross action boundaries.
method: The paper defines exact action-sufficient compression via policy equivalence and approximate sufficiency via bounded expected policy regret, leading to a rate-distortion problem with regret distortion.
result: The optimal stochastic action channel follows a Gibbs distribution, and action adequacy is distinguished from reconstruction fidelity, information-bottleneck prediction, and rational inattention.
conclusion: Robust single-cycle arbitration requires preserving only action-relevant distinctions, not full support, and the rate-regret framework provides a principled compression method.

title: The Bioelectrical Information Theory: Investigating The Theoretical Compression Limit Of Bioelectrical Signals Under Artificial Intelligence
authors: Bo Yan Jiawen Zou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bioelectrical signals are increasingly acquired at scales that challenge the bandwidth of brain-computer interfaces. However, their compression is still often framed as a problem of waveform preservation, limited by the entropy of the raw signal. Here we propose an information-theoretic framework in which the effective information of bioelectrical data is determined not only by signal fidelity, but also by physiological structure, model capacity and downstream task requirements. We formulate bioelectrical compression as a three-level hierarchy. At the signal level, noise is reduced to the information they carry about latent physiological sources. At the physiological level, parametric encoders map purified signals into compact, structured and quantized representations. At the semantic level, task-irrelevant information is discarded, while deep learning models exploit causal dependencies to replace marginal entropy with conditional entropy. This perspective reframes the compression limit of bioelectrical signals as a model- and task-conditioned quantity rather than a fixed property of the waveform. As increasingly expressive models become integrated with neural and physiological interfaces, bioelectrical compression may shift from transmitting signals to transmitting only the residual information required for task-level interpretation.
tldr: Proposes an information-theoretic framework for compressing bioelectrical signals based on physiological structure, model capacity, and task requirements.
motivation: Bioelectrical signal compression is currently limited by raw signal entropy, but the effective information depends on downstream tasks and models.
method: Formulates a three-level hierarchy (signal, physiological, semantic) using parametric encoders and deep learning to discard task-irrelevant information.
result: The compression limit is shown to be a model- and task-conditioned quantity, not a fixed property of the waveform.
conclusion: Future bioelectrical compression may transmit only residual information needed for task-level interpretation.

title: Bridging Scales: Asymptotic Analysis And AI-Assisted Formalization
authors: Xu Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Asymptotic analysis is one of the classical tools for bridging models across scales. Behind many such derivations lies a common symbolic structure: an ansatz, a substitution, an order-by-order matching procedure, and the extraction of effective equations or interface conditions. This article revisits that structure through two representative bridges: the kinetic-to-fluid limit, illustrated by radiative transfer with interface layers and by neural-network approximations of Boltzmann equations, and the quantum-to-classical limit, illustrated by the Frozen Gaussian Approximation and its Dirac extension. We then explain why such derivations are natural candidates for AI-assisted formalization: their recurring symbolic structures can be organized, verified, and reused. In this sense, a carefully structured expository paper may serve not only as a review, but also as a mathematical seed for future AI-assisted environments.
tldr: This paper discusses asymptotic analysis as a tool for bridging scales, with examples from kinetic-to-fluid and quantum-to-classical limits, and proposes AI-assisted formalization of such derivations.
motivation: The author aims to highlight the common symbolic structure in asymptotic derivations across different fields and to argue that these structures are suitable for AI-assisted formalization.
method: The paper revisits two representative bridges: the kinetic-to-fluid limit (radiative transfer with interface layers, neural-network approximations of Boltzmann equations) and the quantum-to-classical limit (Frozen Gaussian Approximation and its Dirac extension).
result: The paper identifies recurring symbolic patterns in asymptotic analysis and suggests that these can be organized, verified, and reused in AI-assisted environments.
conclusion: The author concludes that a carefully structured expository paper can serve as a mathematical seed for future AI-assisted formalization of asymptotic derivations.

title: Minimum Distortion Quantization With Specified Output Distribution
authors: Aolin Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the optimal quantizer of a real-valued random variable [MATH] with distribution [MATH] such that 1) the distribution of the quantization output [MATH] that can take [MATH] values follows any specified distribution [MATH] over [MATH], and 2) the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) of estimating [MATH] from [MATH] is minimized. It is shown that the optimal quantizer takes the form [MATH], where [MATH] is the optimal permutation of [MATH] among all permutations to minimize the MMSE, and [MATH] is the cumulative distribution function. When [MATH] is uniform over an interval or [MATH] is uniform over [MATH], the quantizer takes a simple form [MATH]. The concept of majorization plays a key role in the optimality proof. Specifying the output distribution is useful for designing quantizers with explicitly controlled output entropy, maximized mutual information between input and output, tailored output distribution to match channel input requirements for communication, and data anonymization.
tldr: This paper derives the optimal quantizer that minimizes mean squared error while achieving a specified output distribution, using majorization theory.
motivation: Quantization with controlled output distribution is useful for entropy control, mutual information maximization, channel matching, and data anonymization.
method: The optimal quantizer is shown to be a composition of the cumulative distribution function and an optimal permutation, with majorization used in the proof.
result: The optimal quantizer takes the form Q(x)=π(F(x)) where π is the optimal permutation; for uniform input or output distributions, it simplifies to a linear form.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing quantizers with prescribed output distributions, with potential applications in communication and privacy.

title: Secure Aggregation With Top-K Sparsification In Decentralized Federated Learning
authors: Hengxuan Tang, Jinbao Zhu, Xiaohu Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure aggregation is a vital component for mitigating gradient leakage in federated learning, but its communication cost conventionally scales with the gradient dimension. This becomes prohibitive for large models and even more pronounced in decentralized federated learning with limited bandwidth and unreliable nodes. Top-K gradient sparsification is an effective approach to reduce communication by transmitting only a few entries of the full gradient, while maintaining competitive model accuracy. Nevertheless, the top-K entries selected by each user are unpredictable and vary across users, which poses a challenge for efficient sparse secure aggregation. This paper studies information-theoretic secure aggregation with top-K sparsification in decentralized federated learning under user dropouts and user collusion. We propose a communication-efficient sparse secure aggregation scheme that offloads dimension-dependent overhead to an offline phase and protects private gradients using random masks and permutations. Experimental results demonstrate that our scheme preserves accuracy comparable to full-gradient aggregation even with only 1% gradient sparsification, while substantially reducing the communication cost.
tldr: This paper proposes a communication-efficient secure aggregation scheme with top-K sparsification for decentralized federated learning.
motivation: Secure aggregation in federated learning suffers from high communication cost scaling with gradient dimension, especially in decentralized settings with limited bandwidth and unreliable nodes.
method: The scheme offloads dimension-dependent overhead to an offline phase and protects private gradients using random masks and permutations, enabling efficient sparse secure aggregation.
result: Experiments show that the scheme preserves accuracy comparable to full-gradient aggregation even with 1% gradient sparsification, while substantially reducing communication cost.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively reduces communication overhead in decentralized federated learning without compromising model accuracy.

title: Crossover Of Quasi-localized Dynamics And Diffusion In Supercooled Liquids
authors: Federico Caporaletti
Simone Capaccioli
Dimitrios Bessas
Aleksandr I. Chumakov
Alessandro Martinelli
Francesco Dallari
Giulio Monaco
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the crossover between quasi-localized dynamics and diffusion in supercooled liquids using time-domain interferometry.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic dynamics of glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics, with implications for the glass transition.
method: Time-domain interferometry experiments were performed on a typical glass former to probe fast localized motions and slower diffusive dynamics.
result: The two dynamical processes are found to be coupled, showing a crossover between quasi-localized and diffusive behavior.
conclusion: The coupling of fast and slow dynamics provides new insight into the nature of the glass transition.

title: Superconductivity On Two Surfaces
authors: Tingxin Li
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Superconductivity observed in rhombohedral multilayer graphene with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in a two-surface system where electron and hole layers are separated.
method: Experimental study of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, measuring transport properties.
result: Superconductivity emerges from a normal state with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
conclusion: The two-surface geometry provides a new platform for studying superconductivity.

title: Superconductivity From Dual-surface Carriers In Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Manish Kumar
Derek Waleffe

title: Watching Ionization In A New Light

Renkai Li

method: Experimental demonstration using MeV electron pulses and optical transmission measurement in common semiconductors.
result: Observation of surprisingly strong modulation enabling sub-10-ps timing precision at room temperature.
conclusion: The findings could lead to improved medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
authors: Xuefeng Jiang
Lin Chang
Jing Zhang
Jan Wiersig
Martina Hentschel
Xingjun Wang
Hui Cao
Yun-Feng Xiao
Andrea Alù
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of chaotic photonics in microresonators, focusing on harnessing chaotic dynamics for photonic applications.
motivation: Chaotic dynamics in microcavities can be harnessed for novel photonic technologies, but a comprehensive survey across materials and architectures is lacking.
method: The authors review recent advances in chaotic microcavity photonics, covering various materials and resonator geometries, and discuss how chaos can be controlled and utilized.

result: Determined the CEF energy levels and low-temperature magnetic behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the magnetic frustration and disorder in this material.

title: Many-body Skyrmion Interactions In Helimagnets
authors: N. P. Vizarim, J. C. Bellizotti Souza, Raí M. Menezes, Clécio C. de Souza Silva, P. A. Venegas, And M. V. Milošević
abstract:
