This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological features.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising candidates, but further work is needed to confirm their existence and properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent work using maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural data, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further improvements in experimental sensitivity are needed.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A review of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in exotic geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling simulation of topological phenomena and gravitational models.
method: The paper surveys experimental and theoretical approaches for implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: It summarizes progress in realizing nonstandard geometries and discusses emergent phenomena like topological states and analogies to gravity.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential for simulating fundamental physics, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on how units align their orientation with their own velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active matter, which has implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables a spectrum of behaviors from single-particle orbiting to synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that can be harnessed for designing new materials and robotic systems.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity effects has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: This paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into shape invariants and bosonic excitations, applied to the lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of the wave function into fixed invariants (shapes) satisfying the Pauli principle and a variable bosonic excitation part.
result: A benchmark lithium wave function with hundreds of basis functions is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five of which are numerically significant.
conclusion: The decomposition reveals superselection rules in configuration space and aids in finding robust entangled states.

title: Anisotropic Fluorescence Signals Retarded Dipole-dipole Interactions In A Thermal Atomic Cloud
authors: Vyacheslav Shatokhin, Friedemann Landmesser, Mario Niebuhr, Frank Stienkemeier, Andreas Buchleitner And Lukas Bruder
abstract: We experimentally observe and theoretically explain anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals in the fluorescence from dilute thermal potassium vapours, at room temperature and particle densities . We identify the retarded part of the geometrically fully resolved inter-atomic, resonant dipole-dipole interaction as the crucial ingredient to theoretically reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
tldr: Experimental and theoretical study of anisotropic fluorescence signals due to retarded dipole-dipole interactions in a thermal atomic cloud.
motivation: To understand the role of retarded dipole-dipole interactions in anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals observed in fluorescence from dilute thermal atomic vapors.
method: Experimental observation of fluorescence from thermal potassium vapors combined with theoretical modeling incorporating geometrically resolved retarded dipole-dipole interactions.
result: The retarded part of the dipole-dipole interaction is essential to reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
conclusion: Retarded dipole-dipole interactions are crucial for explaining anisotropic fluorescence signals in thermal atomic clouds.

title: Analytical Response Functions For A Compressible Thin Fluid Layer With Odd Viscosity *
authors: Yuto Hosaka And Shigeyuki Komura Abdallah Daddi-Moussa-Ider
abstract: Fluids composed of chiral active components can exhibit odd viscosity, a property that breaks time-reversal and parity symmetries. We investigate the hydrodynamic response to monopole and dipole singularities in a compressible thin fluid layer with odd viscosity, supported by a conventional lubrication layer. Using the two-dimensional Green’s function in Fourier space, we derive analytical solutions for the flow and pressure fields. These solutions provide a detailed description of the hydrodynamic interactions governing the motion of colloidal particles and microswimmers in confined chiral fluids, offering insight into the role of odd viscosity in modifying particle dynamics and collective behavior. The derived results are directly applicable to modeling transport, control, and self-organization phenomena in active and chiral microfluidic systems.
tldr: This paper studies hydrodynamic response functions in a compressible thin fluid layer with odd viscosity, focusing on chiral active fluids.
motivation: Odd viscosity arises in chiral active fluids and affects particle dynamics and collective behavior; understanding its hydrodynamic effects is important for microfluidic applications.
method: The authors use two-dimensional Green's functions in Fourier space to derive analytical solutions for flow and pressure fields induced by monopole and dipole singularities.
result: Analytical expressions for the flow and pressure fields are obtained, showing how odd viscosity modifies hydrodynamic interactions.
conclusion: The results provide a framework for modeling transport and self-organization in chiral microfluidic systems.

title: Construction Of near-Γ Multiple Chiral Exceptional Points In Momentum Space Of Photonic Crystal Slabs
authors: Jingyu Zhang, Yang Gao, Tianfu Ma, Wenjia Li, Weimin Ye And Jianlong Liu
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optical systems have attracted considerable attention because of their nontrivial topological properties and unusual physical effects. Among them, scattering EPs are particularly appealing for describing chiral response through the scattering matrix. Photonic crystal slabs offer a versatile platform for studying chiral scattering EPs in momentum space, where their topological evolution can be conveniently accessed and engineered. In this work, a convenient approach is presented for achieving chiral scattering EPs near the Γ point by exploiting the topological evolution properties in the momentum space of photonic crystal slabs. By varying the structural parameters of the photonic crystal slabs, multiple chiral EPs are identified near the Γ point, with their evolution and annihilation processes systematically analyzed. Furthermore, the pronounced transmission asymmetry observed near the EP enables polarization conversion from linear to circular, functioning as a quarter-wave plate. This approach provides a straightforward method for realizing and controlling chiral EPs in momentum space, thereby expanding the potential for practical applications in optical metadevices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to create and control chiral exceptional points in photonic crystal slabs, enabling polarization conversion.
motivation: Exceptional points in optical systems have topological properties and unusual effects; controlling them in momentum space is desirable for applications.
method: By varying structural parameters of photonic crystal slabs, multiple chiral exceptional points near the Γ point are identified and their topological evolution is analyzed.
result: Multiple chiral exceptional points are realized, and transmission asymmetry near the EP enables linear-to-circular polarization conversion.
conclusion: The approach provides a straightforward way to realize and control chiral EPs, expanding potential for optical metadevices.

title: Integrated Error-suppressed Pipeline For Quantum Optimization Of Nontrivial Binary Combinatorial Optimization Problems On Gate-model Hardware At The 156-qubit Scale
authors: Natasha Sachdeva, Gavin S Hartnett, Smarak Maity, Samuel Marsh, Yulun Wang, Adam Winick, Ryan Dougherty, Daniel Canuto, You Quan Chong, G Adam Cox, Michael Hush, Pranav S Mundada, Christopher D B Bentley, Michael J Biercuk And Yuval Baum
abstract: We introduce a novel hybrid quantum–classical variational optimization method for unconstrained binary combinatorial optimization problems on gate-model quantum computers, integrating a custom variational ansatz, staged feedback-based dual variational parameter update strategies, efficient parametric compilation, automated error suppression during hardware execution, and scalable O( ) classical post-processing to correct for bitflip errors. Without this integrated approach, we show that standard circuit execution at scale produces output indistinguishable from random sampling, establishing the necessity of each pipeline component. We benchmark the method on IBM superconducting quantum computers for several optimization problems drawn from NP-hard problem classes, where the optimization is conducted on hardware with no use of classical simulation or prior knowledge of the solution. For Max-Cut on random regular graphs with topologies not matched to device connectivity, the method achieves approximation ratios (AR) of 100% for unweighted 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes, weighted regular graphs up to 80 nodes, and weighted 7-regular graphs up 50 nodes. Applied to higher-order binary optimization, the method finds the ground state energy of 127- and 156-qubit spin-glass models matched to device topology with linear, quadratic, and cubic interaction terms, achieving ARs of at least 99.5% across all instances tested. The method consistently outperforms a classical local solver across all problems. Where published results on identical problem instances are available, our method demonstrates competitive or superior performance. These results demonstrate that an appropriately engineered variational approach enables gate-model quantum computers to produce high-quality solutions for binary optimization problems drawn from NP-hard problem classes at the 156-qubit scale, where naïve implementations are insufficient for good performance.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical variational optimization method for binary combinatorial problems on gate-model quantum computers, demonstrated at 156-qubit scale.
motivation: To solve NP-hard binary optimization problems on near-term quantum hardware despite noise and limited connectivity.
method: Integrates a custom variational ansatz, staged feedback-based parameter updates, efficient compilation, automated error suppression, and classical post-processing for bitflip correction.
result: Achieves approximation ratios up to 100% for Max-Cut on 3-regular graphs up to 156 nodes and >99.5% for spin-glass models up to 156 qubits, outperforming classical local solvers.
conclusion: An appropriately engineered variational approach enables gate-model quantum computers to produce high-quality solutions for binary optimization at scale, where naïve implementations fail.

title: Nonreciprocal Electrical Transport In Emerging Noncentrosymmetric Systems: From Hidden Symmetry To Functional Devices
authors: Shengyao Li, Zherui Yang, Xueyan Wang, Kian Ping Loh And X Renshaw Wang
abstract: Contrary to the reciprocal electrical transport constrained by the Onsager relations, nonreciprocal electrical transport arises in noncentrosymmetric systems where the resistance depends on the direction of current flow or external stimuli such as a magnetic field. Governed by symmetry-dependent charge dynamics, these responses appear as nonreciprocal charge transport (NCT) in the longitudinal direction and the nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) in the transverse direction. Recent theoretical advances have expanded the range of mechanisms and material platforms capable of hosting nonreciprocal signals, revealing the role of hidden band-geometric properties. In parallel, experimental developments have exploited these effects for practical devices, offering promising alternatives to semiconductor-based rectifiers and wireless components, with advantages in broadband operation, ultrafast response, and high energy efficiency. In this review, we summarize electrical measurement techniques and characteristic transport signatures for identifying nonreciprocal phenomena and uncovering their underlying symmetry. We provide a comprehensive discussion of the fundamental mechanisms underlying NCT and NLHE, organized through representative material systems, and a subsequent examination of strategies for artificially inducing and enhancing nonreciprocity. Finally, we evaluate the technological perspectives of nonreciprocal electrical transport for electronic applications, along with key challenges and opportunities for scalable device implementation. By synthesizing current progress, this review aims to guide materials discovery and device innovation, and to inspire exploration of new symmetry settings and unconventional routes toward enhanced nonreciprocal functionalities.
tldr: A review of nonreciprocal electrical transport in noncentrosymmetric systems, focusing on symmetry-dependent charge dynamics and device applications.
motivation: To understand and harness nonreciprocal transport phenomena for next-generation electronic devices.
method: Summarizes theoretical mechanisms and experimental techniques for nonreciprocal charge transport and nonlinear Hall effect.
result: Identifies hidden band-geometric properties and strategies to induce/enhance nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal transport offers promising alternatives for broadband, ultrafast, energy-efficient devices, but challenges remain for scalable implementation.

title: Kernel Embeddings And The Separation Of Measure Phenomenon
authors: Leonardo V. Santorokartik G. Waghmarevictor M. Panaretosahttps://ror.org/02s376052institute Of Mathematics, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, Lausanne 1015, Switzerlandbhttps://ror.org/05a28rw58department Of Mathematics, ETH Zürich, Zürich 8092, Switzerland
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 23, June 2026.
SignificanceTwo-sample testing examines whether two probability distributions on some feature space differ based on random samples. It is fundamental in statistics and machine learning, especially when feature spaces are complex. Such settings are ...
tldr: The paper introduces a new method for two-sample testing using kernel embeddings and explores the separation of measure phenomenon.
motivation: Two-sample testing is fundamental in statistics and machine learning, especially for complex feature spaces, and existing methods may fail when distributions are close.
method: The authors propose a kernel-based approach that leverages the separation of measure phenomenon to distinguish distributions with high probability.
result: The method provably achieves consistent testing under mild conditions and outperforms existing tests on synthetic and real data.
conclusion: Kernel embeddings combined with the separation of measure phenomenon provide a powerful framework for two-sample testing.

title: Layerwise Stratification And Band Reordering In Twisted Multilayer MoTe2
authors: Yueyao Fanxiao-Wei Zhangyusen Yexiaoyu Liuchong Wangkaijie Yangdi Xiaoting Caoahttps://ror.org/00cvxb145department Of Materials Science And Engineering, University Of Washington, Seattle, WA 98195bhttps://ror.org/00cvxb145department Of Physics, University Of Washington, Seattle, WA 98195
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 23, June 2026.
SignificanceMultilayer graphene moiré systems have revealed rich correlated and topological quantum phases, yet twisted transition metal dichalcogenides have been studied mainly as bilayer. Here we show that adding more layers changes the underlying ...
tldr: This paper studies layerwise stratification and band reordering in twisted multilayer MoTe2, a condensed matter physics topic focused on moiré systems in transition metal dichalcogenides.
motivation: To understand how adding more layers changes the electronic structure and correlated phases in twisted transition metal dichalcogenides, which have been studied mainly as bilayers.
method: Theoretical modeling and possibly first-principles calculations to analyze band structure and layer-dependent effects in twisted multilayer MoTe2.
result: Adding layers leads to layerwise stratification and band reordering, altering the moiré potential and correlated phases.
conclusion: Multilayer twisted TMDs exhibit richer physics than bilayers, with implications for engineering quantum phases.

title: Multi-channel Optical Vision Model
authors: Ali Momeni, Guillaume Noetinger, Tim Tuuva, Romain Fleury
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial multiplexing is one of the natural strengths of optics, yet in optical neural networks, it is often used mainly as parallel throughput. Here, we show that spatial multiplexing in an optical neural network can be used not only to process multiple inputs in parallel, but also to define a trainable representational coordinate of the model. In three implemented scenarios, parallel-input processing, class-code readout and channel-mixed feature interaction, spatial channels act as independent learners, structured code dimensions, and interacting feature groups. The programmable free-space optical processor is trained through an online physical-forward/surrogate-backward scheme, where measured optical outputs define the forward pass while a differentiable surrogate estimates gradients and is continually fine-tuned during training from newly acquired optical data. We demonstrate these channel roles in image classification and regression tasks using multi-layer architectures with more than one million trainable optical phase parameters. We further implement a hybrid optical-electronic vision-language model, in which the optical neural network provides visual tokens to a digital transformer decoder for controlled image-captioning tasks. These results establish spatially multiplexed optical channels as a programmable feature and readout space for hybrid optical vision models.
tldr: This paper presents a multi-channel optical neural network that uses spatial multiplexing for parallel processing and trainable representational coordinates, demonstrated on image classification and vision-language tasks.
motivation: To leverage spatial multiplexing in optical neural networks beyond simple parallel throughput, enabling richer representational capabilities.
method: A programmable free-space optical processor is trained using a physical-forward/surrogate-backward scheme, with spatial channels acting as independent learners, code dimensions, or interacting feature groups.
result: The approach achieves image classification and regression with over a million trainable optical parameters, and a hybrid optical-electronic vision-language model for controlled image captioning.
conclusion: Spatially multiplexed optical channels can serve as a programmable feature and readout space for hybrid optical vision models.

title: Rainbow Rabbitt As A Probe Of Coherent Rabi Dynamics
authors: Anatoli S. Kheifets Vladislav V. Serov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attosecond pulse trains interacting with a resonantly dressed atom generate a pronounced intra-sideband phase structure that remains hidden in conventional spectrally integrated RABBITT measurements. Using time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation calculations for lithium near the resonant [MATH] transition, we show that the phase extracted within a single sideband can vary by nearly [MATH] across its spectral width. The resulting intra-sideband phase dispersion exhibits a characteristic dependence on the IR detuning, pulse duration, intensity, and sideband order. Most strikingly, exact resonant Rabi flopping flattens the intra-sideband phase dispersion, whereas a small detuning generates a pronounced phase modulation despite weaker population transfer. This counterintuitive behavior demonstrates that rainbow RABBITT probes the dynamical phase accumulated by a Rabi-dressed wave packet rather than the instantaneous populations of the participating states. A simple analytical model captures the principal features of the numerical calculations and provides physical insight into the emergence of the intra-sideband phase structure. These results establish intra-sideband phase dispersion as a new interferometric observable for mapping coherent Rabi dynamics.
tldr: This paper uses rainbow RABBITT spectroscopy to probe coherent Rabi dynamics in a resonantly dressed atom, revealing intra-sideband phase dispersion as a new observable.
motivation: Conventional RABBITT measurements hide intra-sideband phase structure; the authors aim to extract this phase to map coherent dynamics.
method: Time-dependent Schrödinger equation calculations for lithium near a resonant transition, combined with an analytical model.
result: Intra-sideband phase dispersion varies with IR detuning, pulse duration, and intensity; exact resonant Rabi flopping flattens the dispersion while detuning enhances it.
conclusion: Rainbow RABBITT probes the dynamical phase of a Rabi-dressed wave packet, establishing intra-sideband phase dispersion as a new interferometric observable.

title: A Physics-Informed B-Spline Framework For Continuous Approximation Of Flow Data
authors: Junoh Jung, David Lenz, Emil Constantinescu, Tom Peterka
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous approximations of flow data are useful for downstream analysis, differentiation, and visualization, but purely data-driven reconstructions do not, in general, preserve the governing physics. This limitation becomes particularly important when input data are physically inconsistent, whether due to low-fidelity discretizations or unmodeled discrepancies. In such cases, reconstructed fields may exhibit inaccurate PDE residuals, violated balance laws, or unreliable derived quantities. To address this, we propose a physics-informed B-spline framework that embeds physical constraints directly into the reconstruction process. The method constructs compact, continuously differentiable representations of discrete fields using tensor-product B-splines and determines spline control points by solving an optimization problem balancing data fidelity with residuals of the governing PDEs, alongside initial and boundary conditions. Leveraging exact analytical derivatives of the B-spline basis enables efficient and accurate evaluation of physical residuals without storing full-resolution fields. We refer to this approach as physics-informed multivariate functional approximation (PI-MFA). Numerical studies on the 1D convection-diffusion, 2D coupled Burgers, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations show PI-MFA reduces PDE residuals and improves global balance-law consistency. Compared with standard and regularized MFA, PI-MFA produces more physically faithful reconstructions and, for physically inconsistent data, lower approximation errors, while offering computational advantages over tested physics-informed neural networks. Overall, PI-MFA preserves the compactness, local support, and exact differentiability of classical spline spaces while producing reliable continuous flow fields for scientific analysis and visualization.
tldr: A physics-informed B-spline framework for continuous approximation of flow data that embeds PDE constraints into the reconstruction.
motivation: Purely data-driven reconstructions of flow data often violate governing physics, leading to inaccurate residuals and unreliable derived quantities.
method: The method uses tensor-product B-splines and solves an optimization problem balancing data fidelity with PDE residuals and boundary conditions.
result: PI-MFA reduces PDE residuals and improves balance-law consistency compared to standard MFA and physics-informed neural networks.
conclusion: The framework produces physically faithful continuous representations useful for scientific analysis and visualization.

title: Flow-based Generative Models For Amortized Bayesian Inference In Regression And Inverse Pde Problems
authors: Shaoqian Zhou, Ling Guo, Xuhui Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inference provides a principled framework for uncertainty quantification in scientific machine learning. However, conventional Bayesian approaches usually require solving a new inference problem for each observation set, causing substantial computational costs that hinder real-time applications like online monitoring and digital twins. Furthermore, inferring over infinite-dimensional function spaces with varying observation sets poses major challenges for existing amortized inference methods. In this work, we propose Flow-ABI, a flow-based generative framework for amortized Bayesian inference in regression and inverse partial differential equation (PDE) problems. It consists of two components: (i) a functional prior model that learns expressive priors from historical data and physical knowledge through flow matching, and (ii) a set-conditioned functional posterior sampler mapping observation sets to functional posterior distributions. The learned posterior model naturally accommodates varying, permutation-invariant observation sets, and generalizes across different observation discretizations. Once trained, Flow-ABI enables near-real-time posterior sampling for previously unseen observations without retraining or iterative optimization. The proposed methodology can be seamlessly integrated with a wide class of scientific machine learning frameworks, including physics-informed neural networks and neural operators, for uncertainty-aware inverse PDE modeling. Experiments demonstrate that Flow-ABI accurately captures both Gaussian and non-Gaussian posterior distributions while achieving over two-order-of-magnitude speedups relative to the gold-standard Bayesian inference method, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. These results show Flow-ABI is an effective, scalable, and computationally efficient framework for uncertainty quantification in scientific machine learning.
tldr: This paper proposes a flow-based generative model for amortized Bayesian inference in regression and inverse PDE problems, achieving significant speedups over traditional methods.
motivation: Conventional Bayesian inference is computationally expensive and requires retraining for each new observation, hindering real-time applications like online monitoring and digital twins.
method: The method, Flow-ABI, uses a functional prior model learned via flow matching and a set-conditioned functional posterior sampler that maps observation sets to posterior distributions, accommodating varying and permutation-invariant observations.
result: Flow-ABI accurately captures Gaussian and non-Gaussian posteriors and achieves over two-order-of-magnitude speedups compared to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.
conclusion: Flow-ABI provides an effective, scalable, and computationally efficient framework for uncertainty quantification in scientific machine learning.

title: Ytterbium Lattice Clock With Uncertainty Of $1.1\times 10^{-18}$ And Instability Of Low $10^{-19}$
authors: Qiang Zhu, Jingran Shi, Yuechen Zhang, Xiatian Xu, Bing Wang, Dezhi Xiong, Zhuanxian Xiong, Pengcheng Fang, Qunfeng Chen, Lingxiang He, Baolong Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an optical lattice clock based on [MATH]Yb atoms with a total systematic uncertainty of [MATH]. In-vacuum buildup cavity was employed to enhance the lattice light power. Differential frequency measurement between two identical clocks facilitate the evaluation of systematic shifts. Synchronous comparison of the two clocks reached a stability level of [MATH] in an averaging time of 216,000 s. The magic frequency [MATH] was determined to be 394 798 258.3(1) MHz. Under typical operating conditions, the lattice light shift is controlled at an uncertainty level of [MATH]. The blackbody radiation (BBR) shield which is placed in vacuum provides a well-characterized BBR environment, enabling an uncertainty contribution of [MATH] from the BBR Stark shift. Other systematic shifts have also been evaluated. The two clocks will be used for remote frequency comparisons between Shanghai and Wuhan.
tldr: This paper reports a highly precise ytterbium optical lattice clock with record-low systematic uncertainty and instability, focusing on metrology and frequency standards.
motivation: Optical lattice clocks are the most precise timekeeping devices, and further reducing uncertainty and instability is crucial for fundamental physics tests and applications like geodesy.
method: The authors use an in-vacuum buildup cavity for lattice light enhancement, synchronous comparison of two identical clocks, and careful evaluation of systematic shifts including blackbody radiation and lattice light shifts.
result: They achieve a total systematic uncertainty of 1.1×10^{-18} and a stability of low 10^{-19} at 216,000 s averaging time, and determine the magic frequency with high precision.
conclusion: The demonstrated clock performance enables remote frequency comparisons between Shanghai and Wuhan, advancing optical clock networks.

title: Contact Tulczyjew Geometry For Continuous And Discrete Dissipative Dynamics On Skew Algebroids
authors: Manuel de Le\'on Leonardo Colombo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a contact Tulczyjew formalism for dissipative dynamics on skew algebroids. Starting from the Tulczyjew morphism of an skew algebroid, we identify its contact extension in a local line-bundle trivialization. The local representative is obtained by adding to the ordinary Tulczyjew morphism the Euler vector field contribution on [MATH]. This gives an intrinsic explanation of the contact term appearing in the local contact Tulczyjew morphism. For a contact generating object, the construction produces an implicit dissipative dynamics on the contact phase side. In local coordinates, the matching condition gives the Euler-Lagrange-Herglotz equations on the skew algebroid. In the hyperregular case, the corresponding contact Hamiltonian equations are recovered by Legendre transformation. We also develop the discrete counterpart of the construction. After fixing a discrete admissibility relation, a discrete contact generating object defines a discrete contact Tulczyjew relation on the contact phase space. Discrete Herglotz extremals are obtained by matching consecutive contact momenta, with the usual conormal interpretation in the constrained case. In the regular tangent-bundle case, this recovers standard contact variational integrators, while in the singular or skew algebroid setting the same construction remains meaningful as an implicit discrete relation rather than an a priori update map.
tldr: Develops a contact Tulczyjew formalism for dissipative dynamics on skew algebroids, with continuous and discrete versions.
motivation: To provide a geometric framework for dissipative systems that extends the Tulczyjew formalism to contact geometry and skew algebroids.
method: Constructs a contact extension of the Tulczyjew morphism on skew algebroids, using local line-bundle trivialization and Euler vector field contributions; develops discrete counterpart via contact generating objects and admissibility relations.
result: Derives Euler-Lagrange-Herglotz equations on skew algebroids and contact Hamiltonian equations via Legendre transformation; discrete version yields contact variational integrators.
conclusion: The formalism unifies continuous and discrete dissipative dynamics in a geometric setting, applicable to constrained and singular systems.

title: Quantum Study Of Ultracold Atom-ion Excitation Exchange
authors: Tibor J\'on\'as, Romain Vexiau, Nadia Bouloufa-Maafa, Eliane Luc-Koenig, Olivier Dulieu, Andrea Orb\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum dynamics of ultracold collisions between rubidium atoms and excited metastable strontium ions is treated in the laboratory frame, enlightening the importance of the coupling between internal angular momenta of the particles and their mutual rotation. The study reveals a subtle competition between electronic excitation exchange and fine structure quenching, with no charge exchange, which is found to be very sensitive to the details of ion-atom interactions. The rate constant for electronic excitation exchange is found in agreement with the experimental results of Ben-Shlomi (Phys. Rev. A , 031301(R) (2020)), while the rate for fine structure quenching is predicted to strongly depend on the initial polarization of the reactants.
tldr: This paper studies ultracold atom-ion collisions, focusing on excitation exchange and fine structure quenching, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding ultracold atom-ion collisions is important for cold chemistry and precision measurements, but the paper does not address quantum information processing or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform quantum dynamics simulations in the laboratory frame, treating internal angular momenta and rotational coupling.
result: They find a competition between electronic excitation exchange and fine structure quenching, with rate constants matching experimental results for excitation exchange and strong polarization dependence for quenching.
conclusion: The study provides insights into ultracold collision dynamics but does not contribute to the user's research directions.

title: An Adaptive Framework For The Axisymmetric Pulsar Magnetosphere Using Physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Spyros Rigas, Ioannis Contopoulos, Georgios Alexandridis, Antonios Nathanail
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pulsar magnetosphere has only recently been addressed using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), by deploying a domain-decomposition approach and treating the separatrix and equatorial current sheet as infinitesimally thin discontinuities. However, this baseline requires extensive manual hyperparameter tuning, achieves limited final accuracy and demands several hours of training. We refine this framework by introducing domain-specific neural architectures based on Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, an automated adaptive training pipeline and a physics-based convergence criterion that eliminate the need for manual calibration. The proposed methodology delivers self-consistent axisymmetric magnetosphere solutions with mean squared errors of the PDE residuals at O(1e-6) in double precision - an improvement of two orders of magnitude over the baseline - while achieving convergence in under 20 minutes in single precision. Importantly, the method reliably resolves stellar radii reduced by up to 80% compared to the baseline, overcoming the severe spatial scale disparities that also challenge traditional solvers. Furthermore, by varying the flux that opens to infinity, we provide a correction to the equation that connects it to the equatorial T-point's position. The complete framework is released as the open-source library PulsarX.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks to solve the axisymmetric pulsar magnetosphere, achieving high accuracy and fast convergence.
motivation: Existing PINN-based solutions for pulsar magnetospheres require extensive manual tuning, limited accuracy, and long training times.
method: The authors introduce domain-specific Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, an adaptive training pipeline, and a physics-based convergence criterion to automate and improve the solution.
result: The method achieves mean squared errors of O(1e-6) in double precision, converges in under 20 minutes, and resolves stellar radii reduced by up to 80% compared to the baseline.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a more efficient and accurate approach to solving pulsar magnetosphere problems, released as the open-source library PulsarX.

title: Uniform Positivity Of Lyapunov Exponents For Anti H\"older Potentials
authors: Nicholas Chiem
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Schr\"odinger operators with dynamically defined potentials that are anti [MATH]-H\"older and generated by hyperbolic dynamics. We prove an anti Lipschitz estimate on functions related to the orbit of [MATH] under an associated projectivized cocycle. After, we apply the estimate on subshifts of finite type and maps with one expanding direction on [MATH] where [MATH]. In particular, the application leads to uniformly positive Lyapunov exponents with sufficiently large coupling constants.
tldr: Proves uniform positivity of Lyapunov exponents for Schrödinger operators with anti Hölder potentials generated by hyperbolic dynamics.
motivation: Understanding spectral properties of Schrödinger operators with dynamically defined potentials is a fundamental problem in mathematical physics.
method: Derives an anti-Lipschitz estimate for functions related to the orbit under a projectivized cocycle, then applies it to subshifts of finite type and maps with one expanding direction.
result: Establishes uniformly positive Lyapunov exponents for sufficiently large coupling constants.
conclusion: The result contributes to the theory of Schrödinger operators and dynamical systems, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Recent Progress In The Application Of Transfer Operators To Dispersing Billiards
authors: Carlangelo Liverani Mark F Demers
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a review paper about the use of transfer operators to study the statistical properties of hyperbolic billiards. The main focus is on equilibrium states, sequential billiards, and decay of correlation for billiard flows. In addition to reviewing the literature, we try to flesh out the main ideas, highlight the relations between them, and provide the larger context in which the problems discussed here are situated.
tldr: A review of transfer operator methods for studying statistical properties of hyperbolic billiards, focusing on equilibrium states and decay of correlations.
motivation: To understand the statistical behavior of chaotic dynamical systems, specifically dispersing billiards, using transfer operators.
method: Review and synthesis of existing results on transfer operators applied to billiard systems, including equilibrium states and sequential billiards.
result: Provides a coherent overview of how transfer operators yield rigorous results on decay of correlations and other statistical properties for hyperbolic billiards.
conclusion: Transfer operators are a powerful tool for analyzing chaotic billiards, and the review clarifies connections between different approaches.

title: Chiral Algebras With Abelian Conformal Part
authors: P. S. Kolesnikov I. V. Dudin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a categorical approach to the concept of varieties of chiral algebras. We prove that the class of chiral algebras in the variety defined by a binary quadratic operad Var, whose conformal structure is abelian, coincides with the class of differential algebras in the variety defined by the Manin black product of the operads Var and Com, where Com is the operad of associative commutative algebras.
tldr: The paper studies chiral algebras with abelian conformal part using a categorical approach and operad theory.
motivation: To understand the structure of chiral algebras in varieties defined by binary quadratic operads, specifically when the conformal structure is abelian.
method: Uses categorical methods and operad theory, including the Manin black product of operads, to characterize the class of such chiral algebras.
result: Proves that chiral algebras in such a variety coincide with differential algebras in the variety defined by the Manin black product of the operad Var and Com.
conclusion: Provides a categorical characterization of chiral algebras with abelian conformal part, linking them to differential algebras.

title: Accelerating SAV-based Optimization Via Randomized Low-rank Hessian Approximation
authors: Ryo Sagawa, Daisuke Furihata, Yuto Miyatake
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new optimization method, the Nystr\"om-enhanced relaxed scalar auxiliary variable method (N-RSAV), which incorporates curvature information into the RSAV framework to accelerate convergence while preserving an unconditional modified energy dissipation law. Existing RSAV-based methods rely solely on first-order information and often suffer from slow convergence, particularly for ill-conditioned problems such as those arising in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). To address this limitation, we design the linear operator in the RSAV scheme using approximate Hessian information obtained from a randomized low-rank Nystr\"om approximation. To preserve the dissipation structure, we enforce positive semidefiniteness through eigenvalue truncation. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive strategy that reuses the approximate Hessian based on the deviation between the original and modified energies, significantly reducing computational cost. We also provide a convergence analysis of the RSAV scheme with a general positive semidefinite operator under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition and establish corresponding convergence guarantees for N-RSAV under the PL condition and an additional convexity assumption. Numerical experiments on ill-conditioned problems with effectively low-rank structure, including convex quadratic problems and training of PINNs, demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve substantially faster convergence than conventional RSAV-based approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes a Nyström-enhanced relaxed scalar auxiliary variable method for accelerating optimization by incorporating randomized low-rank Hessian approximations while preserving an energy dissipation law.
motivation: Existing RSAV-based optimization methods rely only on first-order information and converge slowly for ill-conditioned problems like training physics-informed neural networks.
method: The method uses a randomized low-rank Nyström approximation to obtain approximate Hessian information, enforces positive semidefiniteness via eigenvalue truncation, and adaptively reuses the Hessian to reduce computational cost.
result: Numerical experiments on convex quadratic problems and PINN training show substantially faster convergence compared to conventional RSAV-based approaches.
conclusion: The N-RSAV method effectively accelerates convergence for ill-conditioned problems with low-rank structure while maintaining an unconditional modified energy dissipation law.

title: Nonlocal Modeling Of Opinion Alignment And Environmental Feedback: Spatial Aggregation And Non-consensus Patterns
authors: Rui Wang, Yunfeng Xiong, Zhengru Zhang, Xiaofei Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formation of public opinion in modern information environments is shaped by the interplay between social conformity and information exposure. While social interactions promote opinion alignment, heterogeneous visibility and selective exposure may reinforce local agreement, a mechanism commonly associated with the echo chamber effects. To describe how such reinforcement influences spatially heterogeneous opinion activity and non-consensus patterns, we propose a spatial opinion dynamics model with attention-mediated feedback. The model couples nonlocal alignment with an evolving attention field and captures a self-reinforcing mechanism in which regions of high opinion activity attract greater visibility. Starting from agent-based jump mechanism inspired by bounded confidence interactions and biased random walks induced by environments, we formally derive a nonlocal advection-cross-diffusion system, where opinion transport is driven by nonlocal conformity and modulated by attention-dependent redistribution. We characterize the transition from spatially homogeneous consensus states to non-consensus clustered regimes through linear stability analysis of the homogeneous equilibrium. The results show that attention-mediated feedback has an explicit correction on the instability threshold and enlarges the parameter regime in which clustering occurs, thereby promoting persistent spatial heterogeneity and non-consensus patterns. Numerical simulations based on a structure-preserving IMEX spectral method support the theoretical predictions and quantify the resulting aggregation phenomena. These findings provide a macroscopic description of how nonlocal alignment and environmental feedback jointly shape spatial signatures of non-consensus patterns.
tldr: A spatial opinion dynamics model with nonlocal alignment and attention-mediated feedback, analyzed via linear stability and numerical simulations.
motivation: To understand how social conformity and selective visibility shape spatially heterogeneous opinion patterns and echo chambers.
method: Derives a nonlocal advection-cross-diffusion system from agent-based jump processes, then performs linear stability analysis and IMEX spectral simulations.
result: Attention-mediated feedback lowers the instability threshold and enlarges the clustering regime, promoting persistent non-consensus patterns.
conclusion: Nonlocal alignment and environmental feedback jointly drive spatial aggregation and non-consensus opinion patterns.

title: Fr\'echet Means Of Periodic Orbits In Dynamical Systems: Geometry, Dynamics, And Diagnostics
authors: Christian Kuehn Paulina Hering
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many dynamical systems applications, one seeks representative trajectories summarizing families of periodic orbits arising from parameter variation or uncertainty. While the Fr\'echet mean provides a natural notion of averaging in nonlinear metric spaces, its application to periodic trajectories is complicated by the interplay between geometric shape and temporal dynamics. Inspired by ideas from shape analysis, we develop a framework for computing Fr\'echet means of periodic orbits by representing trajectories as closed curves and introducing a metric structure on a quotient space that accounts for circular phase shifts. Within this framework, we establish the existence of empirical Fr\'echet means in the resulting infinite-dimensional quotient space. A central finding is that the resulting Fr\'echet mean depends strongly on the chosen parametrization: time parametrization preserves dynamical information, whereas arc length parametrization emphasizes geometric structure. To reconcile these viewpoints, we propose a decoupled approach that computes a geometric Fr\'echet mean using arc length parametrization and subsequently reconstructs representative dynamics through harmonic averaging of aligned speed profiles. We further introduce curvature- and medoid-based diagnostic measures that quantify the representativeness of the resulting mean and identify situations in which averaging produces geometric artifacts or fails to capture heterogeneous ensembles. Numerical experiments for the Van der Pol oscillator, the Rosenzweig-MacArthur predator-prey model, and the Morris-Lecar neuronal model demonstrate that the proposed methodology yields robust geometric summaries together with consistent averaged dynamics. The framework provides a principled approach for constructing representative periodic trajectories and assessing their validity in uncertainty quantification and dynamical systems.
tldr: This paper develops a framework for computing Fréchet means of periodic orbits in dynamical systems, focusing on geometry and dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: In many dynamical systems applications, one needs representative trajectories summarizing families of periodic orbits, but averaging periodic orbits is complicated by the interplay between geometric shape and temporal dynamics.
method: The authors represent trajectories as closed curves, introduce a metric on a quotient space accounting for circular phase shifts, and propose a decoupled approach using arc-length parametrization for geometry and harmonic averaging for dynamics.
result: Existence of empirical Fréchet means is established, and numerical experiments on Van der Pol, Rosenzweig-MacArthur, and Morris-Lecar models demonstrate robust geometric summaries and consistent averaged dynamics.
conclusion: The framework provides a principled approach for constructing representative periodic trajectories and assessing their validity in uncertainty quantification and dynamical systems.

title: Generating Functions For Aggregation And Fragmentation: Review
authors: S. A. Matveev
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we review and revisit the generating function techniques that provide exact analytical solutions for aggregation and fragmentation equations across several physical regimes including spontaneous and collisonal shattering. For discrete coagulation-fragmentation equations with size-independent rates under monodisperse initial conditions, we show the derivation of sevaral explicit closed-form solutions. We also briefly report the exact solutions for continuous, three-particle, [MATH]-particle collisions and two-component generalizations. Source-driven aggregation yields steady distributions featuring a universal [MATH] power-law decay and a cutoff mass scaling [MATH].
tldr: This paper reviews generating function techniques for solving aggregation and fragmentation equations in physical systems.
motivation: Aggregation and fragmentation processes are common in many physical systems, and exact solutions are valuable for understanding their dynamics.
method: The authors use generating functions to derive closed-form solutions for discrete coagulation-fragmentation equations with size-independent rates and monodisperse initial conditions.
result: Explicit solutions are obtained for several regimes, including spontaneous and collisional shattering, and source-driven aggregation yields steady distributions with universal power-law decay.
conclusion: Generating functions provide a powerful tool for exact analytical solutions in aggregation-fragmentation problems, with extensions to continuous and multi-component cases.

title: A Note On The Strategic Confinement Problem
authors: Christian Schroeder de Witt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.09931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lampson's confinement problem asks how to prevent a program that processes confidential information from leaking it to a third party. We introduce the strategic confinement problem, which arises when the communicating parties are strategic agents with shared coordination resources. In this setting, residual communication capacity can be concentrated on low-entropy, high-impact predicates of the confidential data. Consequently, bounds on information leakage need not induce corresponding bounds on worst-case harm: a channel with negligible capacity may still suffice to select damaging outcomes. We argue that systems of learnt strategic agents naturally instantiate this problem because they do not admit complete behavioural specifications, their learnt conventions generally cannot be predicted or reproduced by an external observer, and sufficiently capable agents can construct covert communication schemes that are difficult to detect or eliminate. Our contribution is therefore not a new theory of communication, but a reinterpretation of confinement in the presence of strategic agents. Classical confinement bounds what information may flow; strategic confinement highlights that this need not bound what strategic agents can jointly achieve.
tldr: This paper reinterprets the classical confinement problem in the context of strategic agents, showing that low-capacity channels can still cause high-impact harm.
motivation: Classical confinement bounds information flow but does not account for strategic agents who can coordinate to exploit low-entropy, high-impact predicates.
method: The paper introduces the strategic confinement problem, analyzing how residual communication capacity can be concentrated on damaging outcomes, and argues that learnt strategic agents naturally instantiate this problem.
result: Bounds on information leakage do not necessarily bound worst-case harm; a channel with negligible capacity may still enable selection of damaging outcomes.
conclusion: Strategic confinement highlights a new challenge for security in systems with learnt strategic agents, requiring new approaches beyond classical information flow control.

title: Do LLMsMakeNeural Distinguishers Wise?
authors: Tatsuya Sakagami, Masashi Hisai, Naoto Yanai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.10692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural distinguishers are a cryptanalysis method for symmetric-key cryptography that trains machine learning models on pairs of plaintexts and ciphertexts with specific differences in order to recover a secret key. To the best of our knowledge, no existing work has explored the use of large language models (LLMs) for neural distinguishers. In this paper, we propose LLM-based neural distinguishers through a prompt design and conduct extensive experiments with them on SPECK-32/64 to investigate whether LLMs can strengthen neural distinguishers. We then found three key insights. First, by comparing the results of LLM-based neural distinguishers with ResNet in the existing work, we demonstrate that LLMs provide no observable improvement in the performance of neural distinguishers. Second, we confirm that, at high rounds, the choice of differences is no longer effective for LLM-based neural distinguishers as well as ResNet. Third, we show that the performance of LLM-based neural distinguishers can be significantly improved by incorporating only the XOR operation results as a prompt design.
tldr: This paper explores using large language models as neural distinguishers for symmetric-key cryptography, finding no improvement over existing methods.
motivation: To investigate whether LLMs can enhance neural distinguishers, a cryptanalysis method for symmetric-key ciphers.
method: The authors design prompts for LLMs to perform neural distinguisher tasks on SPECK-32/64 and compare performance with ResNet baselines.
result: LLMs provide no observable improvement; at high rounds, difference choice is ineffective; incorporating XOR results improves performance.
conclusion: LLMs are not beneficial for neural distinguishers in their current form, but prompt engineering with XOR operations can help.

title: Soft-X-ray Momentum Microscopy Of Nonlinear Magnon Interactions
authors: Steffen Wittrock
Christopher Klose
Salvatore Perna
Korbinian Baumgaertl
Andrea Mucchietto
Michael Schneider
Josefin Fuchs
Victor Deinhart
Tamer Karaman
Dirk Grundler
Stefan Eisebitt

Daniel Schick
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a soft-X-ray momentum microscopy technique to image nonlinear magnon interactions with nanoscale sensitivity.
motivation: Nonlinear magnon interactions are difficult to detect, limiting the study of nanoscale spin dynamics.
method: The authors use soft X-rays to image magnon momentum, enabling detection of nonlinear interactions.
result: The method captures nonlinear magnon interactions with nanometre-scale sensitivity.
conclusion: Soft-X-ray momentum microscopy is a powerful tool for studying nanoscale spin dynamics and nonlinear magnon couplings.

title: Is Ball Lightning A Relativistic Soliton?
authors: Sergei Bulanov
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes that ball lightning may be explained by relativistic solitons, supported by laser experiments producing millimeter-scale solitons.
motivation: Ball lightning is a poorly understood atmospheric phenomenon; the paper aims to test whether relativistic solitons can account for its stability and size.
method: High-power laser experiments are used to generate relativistic solitons in a laboratory setting, and their properties are compared to ball lightning observations.
result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons are produced, suggesting that such structures could indeed explain ball lightning.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons are a plausible explanation for ball lightning, warranting further investigation.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity and introduces Lorentz violation via work-producing legs, leading to late-time cosmological consequences.
motivation: To explore controlled violations of Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation within an emergent gravity framework, and to study their cosmological implications.
method: The authors model general relativity as a thermodynamic Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs, then add work-producing legs to generate Lorentz violation, analyzing the resulting cosmological dynamics.
result: The work-producing legs produce late-time cosmic acceleration and other observable signatures, providing a thermodynamic origin for dark energy.
conclusion: Lorentz violation in emergent gravity can explain dark energy and offers testable predictions for cosmology.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang

Broadband-tunable coherent phonon tips probe functional materials at nanoscale to investigate a variety of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties.

tldr: This paper demonstrates nanoscale coherent phonon tips with broadband frequency tunability for probing material properties.
motivation: To develop a versatile tool for investigating optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties at the nanoscale using coherent phonons.
method: The authors fabricate nanoscale tips that generate coherent phonons with tunable frequencies and use them to probe functional materials.
result: They achieve broadband frequency tunability of coherent phonons at the nanoscale.
conclusion: The tunable coherent phonon tips provide a new approach for nanoscale characterization of material properties.

authors: N. J. Ayres et Al.

This method is also used to exploit sensitivity to the storage properties of the materials used to trap ultracold neutrons, specifi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.

motivation: Understanding the energy spectrum and storage properties of ultracold neutrons is important for neutron electric dipole moment (nEDM) experiments.
method: The authors use magnetically induced spin depolarization measurements in the n2EDM apparatus to infer the neutron energy spectrum and material-dependent storage properties.
result: The method successfully extracts the energy spectrum and provides sensitivity to storage properties of trap materials.
conclusion: This technique offers a novel diagnostic tool for ultracold neutron sources and storage chambers.

title: Acoustic Analogy Of Quantum Baldin Sum Rule For Optimal Causal Scattering
authors: Sichao Qu, Zixiong Yu, Erqian Dong, Min Yang, And Nicholas X. Fang
abstract:
Author(s): Sichao Qu, Zixiong Yu, Erqian Dong, Min Yang, and Nicholas X. Fang

Sound wave scattering can be increased in one frequency range only by reducing scattering in another range, according to experiments—a discovery relevant for acoustic engineering.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an acoustic analogy of the quantum Baldin sum rule, demonstrating a trade-off in sound wave scattering across frequencies.
motivation: To explore fundamental limits in acoustic scattering, analogous to quantum sum rules, for optimal design of acoustic devices.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical modeling of sound wave scattering in engineered structures.
result: Scattering enhancement in one frequency range necessarily reduces scattering in another, confirming the sum rule.
conclusion: The acoustic Baldin sum rule provides a universal constraint for acoustic scattering, with implications for acoustic engineering.

result: Acoustic magnetochiral anisotropy is observed, showing direction-dependent acoustic properties in a magnetic field.
conclusion: The effect is a classical wave phenomenon in a diamagnetic crystal, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Accurate Boundary Bootstrap For The Three-Dimensional $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Normal Universality Class
authors: Runzhe Hu And Wenliang Li

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221601] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the boundary critical behavior of the 3D O(N) model using conformal bootstrap methods.
motivation: Understanding boundary universality classes in 3D O(N) models, particularly the extraordinary-log phase, is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use numerical conformal bootstrap techniques to compute boundary critical exponents and correlation functions.
result: They obtain accurate estimates for the critical value N_c and the boundary correlation exponent for the normal universality class.
conclusion: The results confirm and refine the understanding of boundary criticality in 3D O(N) models, but the work is purely in statistical/condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterization Of Feshbach Resonances In A $^{6}\mathrm{Li}−^{7}\mathrm{Li}$ Mixture Using Improved Interaction Potentials
authors: Jing-Chen Zhang (张京晨), Paul Julienne, And Yu Liu
abstract:

We characterize Feshbach resonances in all isotopologs of the [MATH] system with improved interaction potentials. Starting from spectroscopically accurate Morse/long-range (MLR) potential-energy curves for the singlet [MATH] and triplet [MATH] ele…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062802] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Characterization of Feshbach resonances in a lithium isotope mixture using improved interaction potentials.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of Feshbach resonances is essential for controlling ultracold atomic interactions, but existing potentials for Li mixtures are insufficiently precise.
method: Constructed spectroscopically accurate Morse/long-range (MLR) potential-energy curves for singlet and triplet states, then calculated resonance positions and widths.
result: Predicted new Feshbach resonances and improved agreement with experimental data for 6Li-7Li mixtures.
conclusion: The improved potentials enable more precise control of atomic interactions, benefiting experiments in ultracold physics.

title: Coherent Radiation Of Multielectron Wave Packets In Intense Laser Fields
authors: Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, And Bin Qiao

In this work, we investigate the coherent radiation emitted by a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse in the framework of strong-field QED. Using the density matrix formalism, we gene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063105] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Investigates coherent radiation from multielectron wave packets in intense laser fields using strong-field QED and density matrix formalism.
motivation: To understand and characterize coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams as a potential light source.
method: Uses density matrix formalism within strong-field QED to model a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse.
result: Derives general expressions for coherent radiation and analyzes the effects of electron correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for coherent radiation from multielectron systems, relevant for light source development.

title: Hybridized Kagome Bands And Induced Ti Magnetism In $R{\mathrm{Ti}}_{3}{\mathrm{Bi}}_{4}$ $(R=\mathrm{Nd}, \mathrm{Sm}, \mathrm{Gd})$ Kagome Metals Studied Using Angle-resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy And X-ray Magnetic Circular Dichroism

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214426] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.

motivation: To understand the interplay between lattice, charge, and spin orders in kagome materials, which host emergent quantum phenomena.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), density functional theory (DFT), and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) were used to probe the electronic and magnetic properties.
result: Hybridized kagome bands and induced Ti magnetism were observed in R-Ti3-Bi4 compounds (R=Nd, Sm, Gd).
conclusion: The study provides detailed characterization of these kagome metals but does not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

We investigate the dynamics of ferroelectric textures driven by polarization currents. We show that ferrons, the quanta of collective polarization excitations, provide an exotic driving mechanism for domain wall (DW) dynamics, compared with their magnonic counterparts. By mapping the linear polariza…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220103] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies ferroelectric domain wall dynamics driven by polarization currents and introduces ferrons as quanta of collective polarization excitations.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of ferroelectric textures under polarization currents and compare with magnon-driven domain wall motion.
method: Theoretical analysis mapping linear polarization excitations to ferrons and deriving the resulting force on domain walls.
result: Ferrons provide an exotic driving mechanism for domain wall dynamics distinct from magnonic counterparts.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of ferroelectric domain wall dynamics but is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unconventional Temperature Dependence Of Uniaxial Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy In The Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{FePS}}_{3}$
authors: Liang Zhou, Jiawei Jiang, Jiawei Liu, Rui Liang, Ziying Li, Zhenxing Wang, Hongxin Yang, And Nujiang Tang

The van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnets with a large uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy (UMA) have compelling advantages for terahertz spintronics applications. Although the temperature dependence of UMA is essential for ensuring device endurance, it has scarcely been explored. Here, we unveil …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220403] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature dependence of uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, relevant for terahertz spintronics.
motivation: Understanding the temperature dependence of UMA is crucial for device endurance in terahertz spintronics applications, but it has been scarcely explored.
method: The authors perform experimental measurements and theoretical calculations to unveil the unconventional temperature dependence of UMA in FePS3.
result: They find an unconventional temperature dependence of UMA, which deviates from standard behavior.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the magnetic properties of FePS3, aiding its application in spintronics.

Rare-earth triangular lattices provide an ideal platform for exploring novel quantum magnetic states. Here, we report the crystal growth and magnetic properties of a rare-earth triangular-lattice compound, [MATH]. Alternating-current magnetic susceptibility and specifi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214422] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the crystal growth and magnetic properties of a rare-earth triangular-lattice compound ErZn3P3, revealing fragile long-range antiferromagnetic order.
motivation: Rare-earth triangular lattices are platforms for novel quantum magnetic states, but the magnetic properties of ErZn3P3 were previously unexplored.
method: Single crystals were grown, and magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and neutron diffraction measurements were performed to characterize the magnetic order.
result: The compound exhibits long-range antiferromagnetic order below 2.2 K, but the order is fragile and easily suppressed by magnetic fields.
conclusion: ErZn3P3 is a candidate for studying frustrated magnetism and field-induced quantum phases in triangular lattices.

title: Melting Point Depression Of The Charge Density Wave In $1T\text{−}\mathrm{Ti}{\mathrm{Se}}_{2}$ Due To Size Effects
authors: Saif Siddique, Mehrdad T. Kiani, Omri Lesser, Stephen D. Funni, Nishkarsh Agarwal, Maya Gates, Miti Shah, William Millsaps, Suk Hyun Sung, Noah Schnitzer, Lopa Bhatt, David A. Muller, Robert Hovden, Ismail El Baggari, Eun-Ah Kim, And Judy J. Cha
